levels.Proficient: Independently manages executive calendars, agendas, minutes, and follow-through actions.

competencies.name: Vehicle Operation and Driving Support
competencies.definition: Ability to safely and reliably operate an assigned service vehicle in support of Executive Offices transport, errand, and logistics requirements, while observing traffic laws, vehicle care, and basic roadworthiness checks. Benchmarked from General Services Division's Fleet Management competency and adapted to the individual-driver duties performed by Executive Offices administrative aides who serve as drivers, rather than fleet-wide coordination.

dimensions.name: Safe Vehicle Operation
dimensions.definition: Ability to drive assigned service vehicles safely and in compliance with traffic laws and organizational policies.

levels.Emerging: Drives assigned routes and errands safely under close supervision, following basic traffic rules and organizational policies.
levels.Developing: Independently drives routine trips and errands, adjusting to traffic conditions and passenger or cargo requirements.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex or time-sensitive trips, including priority transport, with sound judgment and minimal supervision.
levels.Advanced: Serves as a lead driver for critical or sensitive assignments and guides other drivers on safe operating practices.

dimensions.name: Vehicle Care and Basic Maintenance
dimensions.definition: Ability to perform routine vehicle checks, report issues, and maintain the assigned vehicle in good working condition.

levels.Emerging: Performs basic pre-trip vehicle checks and reports obvious issues to the supervisor.
levels.Developing: Conducts routine vehicle upkeep, such as cleanliness, fluid levels, and tire condition, and coordinates minor repairs.
levels.Proficient: Identifies recurring vehicle issues and recommends preventive maintenance actions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes good vehicle-care practices and mentors other drivers on preventive maintenance.

dimensions.name: Trip Documentation and Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain accurate trip records, fuel logs, and documentation required for official vehicle use.

levels.Emerging: Maintains basic trip tickets and fuel records with guidance.
levels.Developing: Accurately completes trip and fuel documentation for routine assignments.
levels.Proficient: Reviews documentation for completeness and resolves discrepancies.
levels.Advanced: Ensures consistent documentation practices and compliance with vehicle-use policies across assignments.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic road hazards and follows safety instructions.
levels.Developing: Applies defensive driving practices and reports safety concerns.
levels.Proficient: Manages challenging driving conditions, such as weather, traffic, or unfamiliar routes, and responds appropriately to incidents.
levels.Advanced: Models safe driving practices and advises on measures to reduce vehicle-related risks.

competencies.name: Communications Proficiency
competencies.definition: The ability to convey clear, accurate, timely and convincing ideas and information through written, verbal and virtual platforms to support coordination, public information, media engagement, implementation, monitoring and reporting.

dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare and deliver clear, concise and audience-appropriate oral and written communications.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine correspondence and delivers simple information clearly; follows approved communication formats.

levels.Proficient: Drafts and reviews complex reports, messages and technical communications; adjusts messaging to audience and issue.
levels.Advanced: Develops communication strategies, advises senior officials, and coaches others on high-impact communication.

levels.Proficient: Facilitates difficult discussions, manages expectations and negotiates communication approaches.
levels.Advanced: Breaks down communication barriers, resolves complex stakeholder concerns and builds sustained commitment.

dimensions.name: Technical and Executive Communication

levels.Emerging: Gathers information and prepares basic briefs, talking points and reports from available sources.
levels.Developing: Prepares substantive briefs, reports and messages requiring synthesis of several information sources.
levels.Proficient: Develops convincing executive-level materials involving interrelated issues and current developments.
levels.Advanced: Serves as an organizational communication adviser and produces high-level materials for sensitive or strategic matters.

dimensions.name: Communication Quality and Editing
dimensions.definition: Ability to edit, proofread and improve communications for accuracy, clarity, tone and consistency.

levels.Proficient: Designs communication approaches for complex issues and anticipates likely stakeholder reactions.

levels.Advanced: Sets meaningful digital performance measures and uses analytics to direct strategy. Leads digital risk and reputation management and establishes ethical standards for online communication.

dimensions.name: Cash and Accountability Report Preparation
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare required reports using complete, accurate and supported source data.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing routine reports using prescribed formats.
levels.Developing: Prepares routine cash/accountability reports accurately and within deadlines.
levels.Proficient: Prepares or reviews complex reports, validates supporting data and resolves inconsistencies.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert review and establishes reporting controls that improve reliability and timeliness.

dimensions.name: Reconciliation and Data Validation
dimensions.definition: Ability to reconcile cash, checks, collections, deposits, disbursements and related records and identify discrepancies.

levels.Emerging: Performs basic checks and identifies obvious discrepancies with guidance.
levels.Developing: Reconciles routine records and corrects or reports discrepancies.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex reconciliation issues and determines appropriate corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on reconciliation and strengthens preventive controls against recurring discrepancies.

dimensions.name: Commission on Audit (COA), BTr and Regulatory Reporting
dimensions.definition: Ability to validate, route and submit required reports to Commission on Audit (COA), BTr and other authorized recipients within prescribed deadlines.

levels.Emerging: Prepares assigned supporting documents for submission with guidance.
levels.Developing: Processes routine reports for timely and accurate submission.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex submissions, addresses deficiencies and coordinates corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides direction on regulatory reporting compliance and improves submission controls.

dimensions.name: Digital Financial and Banking Reports
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, validate and monitor reports relating to digital payment systems and banking transactions.

levels.Emerging: Assists in compiling assigned digital/banking data for reporting.
levels.Developing: Prepares routine digital/banking reports accurately and on time.
levels.Proficient: Validates complex digital/banking data and resolves inconsistencies across systems and records.
levels.Advanced: Establishes controls and reporting practices that improve integrity of digital financial information.

dimensions.name: Report Accuracy, Completeness and Timeliness
dimensions.definition: Ability to produce complete, accurate, supported and timely reports with minimal avoidable revision.

levels.Emerging: Applies prescribed checking procedures before submission.
levels.Developing: Consistently submits accurate and complete reports within deadlines.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex reports and prevents material errors or revisions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes quality-assurance practices that sustain accurate, complete and timely reporting.

competencies.name: Tax, Fidelity Bond and Statutory Compliance
competencies.definition: The ability to process, validate, monitor and submit tax-related documents, tax certificates, annual tax statements/alphalists, fidelity bond documents and other statutory or regulatory requirements that remain within the Cash Division's assigned functions.

dimensions.name: Tax Withholding Documentation and Certificates
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, validate and issue tax certificates and related withholding documentation within prescribed requirements.

levels.Emerging: Assists in compiling information and checking assigned tax documents/certificates.
levels.Developing: Processes routine tax certificates and withholding documents accurately and on time.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex tax documentation and resolves discrepancies before issuance/submission.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert technical guidance on complex tax-document compliance and improves controls.

dimensions.name: Annual Tax Statements and Alphalists
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, validate and submit annual statements and alphalists of payees reflecting income tax withheld and remitted, where assigned.

levels.Emerging: Assists in compiling data for assigned annual tax statements/alphalists with guidance.
levels.Developing: Prepares assigned annual statements/alphalists accurately using validated source data.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex annual tax reporting, validates data and resolves discrepancies before submission.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction and strengthens controls for reliable annual tax reporting.

dimensions.name: Fidelity Bond Administration
dimensions.definition: Ability to process, validate, monitor and maintain fidelity bond requirements for accountable officers.

levels.Emerging: Assists in checking bond documents and routing them for appropriate action.
levels.Developing: Processes routine bond documentation and maintains monitoring records.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex bond cases and coordinates resolution of deficiencies or delays.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert guidance and strengthens controls for accountable-officer bond compliance.

dimensions.name: Statutory and Regulatory Compliance Monitoring
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor applicable deadlines and ensure required documents and actions are completed, signed and submitted.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine deadlines and follows established compliance schedules.
levels.Developing: Monitors assigned compliance requirements and completes submissions on time.
levels.Proficient: Anticipates compliance risks and coordinates corrective action for complex cases.
levels.Advanced: Provides division-level direction on compliance monitoring and improves systems for sustained compliance.

competencies.name: Financial Documentation, Reportorial and Organizational Support
competencies.definition: The ability to manage financial documentation, reportorial requirements, records, and assigned administrative or organizational support functions accurately, systematically, securely and within prescribed timelines.

dimensions.name: Financial Records and Document Control
dimensions.definition: Ability to organize, maintain, retrieve and safeguard financial documents and supporting records required for transactions, reporting and audit/reference purposes.

levels.Emerging: Files and maintains assigned documents using established procedures.
levels.Developing: Maintains complete, organized and retrievable financial records.
levels.Proficient: Reviews record completeness and resolves documentation gaps affecting transactions or reports.
levels.Advanced: Improves document-control systems and establishes stronger practices for reliability and audit readiness.

dimensions.name: Reportorial and Management Requirements
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare and submit assigned internal and management reportorial requirements accurately and on time.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing routine reportorial submissions with guidance.
levels.Developing: Completes assigned reports accurately and within prescribed deadlines.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates complex reportorial requirements and resolves issues affecting timely submission.
levels.Advanced: Provides direction on reportorial compliance and improves monitoring mechanisms.

dimensions.name: Administrative and Organizational Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to process assigned administrative, employee-support and organizational requirements and coordinate with concerned offices.

levels.Emerging: Processes routine requests using established procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently processes routine support requirements within prescribed timelines.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex requests and coordinates with concerned offices to resolve issues.
levels.Advanced: Improves support processes and provides guidance on complex organizational support matters.

dimensions.name: Digital Records and Information Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain organized, accessible and secure digital records and information supporting cash operations.

levels.Emerging: Files assigned digital records using prescribed naming, storage and access procedures.
levels.Developing: Maintains accurate, organized and retrievable digital records.
levels.Proficient: Identifies data-quality or access issues and resolves documentation gaps affecting operations.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens digital records practices, controls access risks and improves information reliability.

dimensions.name: Learning, Knowledge Sharing and Development Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to participate in learning interventions and apply/share relevant knowledge to improve work practices.

levels.Emerging: Participates in required learning interventions with guidance.
levels.Developing: Completes assigned learning interventions and applies relevant learning to work.
levels.Proficient: Shares or applies learning to improve work practices and supports peers when appropriate.
levels.Advanced: Promotes knowledge sharing, mentoring and application of learning to improve division performance.

competencies.name: Digital Treasury and Electronic Payment Operations
competencies.definition: The ability to operate, monitor, validate and support electronic treasury and payment transactions through authorized digital financial platforms, while maintaining data integrity, security, timeliness and compliance.

dimensions.name: Electronic Payment Platform Processing
dimensions.definition: Ability to process and monitor authorized electronic payments using eMDS, weAccess, eTRA, eTPS and other prescribed platforms.

levels.Emerging: Assists in navigating assigned digital platforms and processing routine transactions with guidance.
levels.Developing: Processes routine electronic payments accurately and within prescribed timelines.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex electronic transactions and resolves platform or transaction exceptions.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction on electronic payment operations and improves digital processing controls.

dimensions.name: Electronic Payroll and Payment Uploads
dimensions.definition: Ability to upload and monitor authorized payroll/payment files through prescribed digital systems.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing or checking files for authorized digital upload.
levels.Developing: Uploads routine payroll/payment files accurately and verifies processing status.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex upload/data issues and coordinates corrective action with concerned offices.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens digital payroll/payment controls and improves reliability of electronic uploads.

dimensions.name: Digital Transaction Monitoring and Exception Handling
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor electronic transactions and identify, document and resolve failed, returned, invalidated or delayed transactions.

levels.Emerging: Monitors assigned transaction status and reports obvious exceptions with guidance.
levels.Developing: Tracks routine electronic transactions and follows prescribed exception-resolution procedures.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes failed/returned/invalidated transactions and coordinates timely corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Establishes monitoring and escalation mechanisms that reduce recurring digital transaction failures.

dimensions.name: Digital Data Integrity and Security
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain accurate transaction data and observe prescribed access, security and control requirements.

levels.Emerging: Follows prescribed access, data-entry and security procedures.
levels.Developing: Maintains accurate digital transaction records and protects assigned system access.
levels.Proficient: Identifies data-integrity/security risks and coordinates appropriate corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens controls for digital data integrity, access management and secure treasury operations.

dimensions.name: TSA and Digital Treasury Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor compliance of electronic disbursements with Treasury Single Account and related treasury requirements.

levels.Emerging: Follows established TSA and digital treasury procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Monitors routine electronic transactions for compliance with prescribed TSA requirements.
levels.Proficient: Identifies complex compliance issues and coordinates resolution with BTr and concerned offices.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on TSA/digital treasury compliance and improves monitoring controls.

competencies.name: Cash Operations Coordination and Banking Liaison
competencies.definition: The ability to coordinate cash operations with operating units, internal offices, authorized government banks, the Bureau of the Treasury, Commission on Audit and other stakeholders; communicate requirements; and facilitate timely resolution of operational issues.

dimensions.name: Internal Cash Operations Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate requirements, schedules, documents and issues with operating units and internal DOTr offices.

levels.Emerging: Provides or receives routine information with guidance.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine cash requirements and schedules with concerned offices.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex cross-office coordination and resolves conflicting requirements.
levels.Advanced: Provides division-level direction on coordination mechanisms and improves inter-office workflows.

dimensions.name: Banking and Treasury Liaison
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate with authorized government banks and BTr on cash, banking, electronic payment and treasury matters.

levels.Emerging: Assists in routine coordination with banks/BTr using established protocols.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine banking and treasury transactions and follow-ups.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex banking/treasury issues and facilitates resolution with relevant parties.
levels.Advanced: Serves as technical resource on significant banking/treasury issues and strengthens liaison arrangements.

dimensions.name: Oversight and Compliance Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate responses, clarifications and documentation with Commission on Audit (COA) and other oversight bodies.

levels.Emerging: Prepares assigned documents or responses with guidance.
levels.Developing: Provides complete and timely information for routine oversight requirements.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates complex clarifications, deficiencies or requests and ensures appropriate response.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on oversight coordination and strengthens readiness for regulatory review.

dimensions.name: Issue Resolution and Escalation
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify operational issues, determine appropriate escalation and facilitate timely resolution.

levels.Emerging: Identifies and reports routine issues to the appropriate personnel.
levels.Developing: Resolves routine operational issues independently and escalates exceptions appropriately.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex issues, coordinates corrective action and follows through to closure.
levels.Advanced: Leads resolution of significant or recurring operational issues and improves escalation mechanisms.

dimensions.name: Stakeholder Communication and Service
dimensions.definition: Ability to communicate cash-operation requirements clearly, professionally and in a manner that supports timely service delivery.

levels.Emerging: Communicates routine requirements clearly with guidance.
levels.Developing: Provides accurate and timely information to stakeholders and follows through on routine requests.
levels.Proficient: Handles sensitive or complex concerns using sound judgment and maintains effective working relationships.
levels.Advanced: Sets service and communication practices that improve stakeholder confidence and operational responsiveness.

competencies.name: Internal Control and Cash Management Process Improvement
competencies.definition: The ability to assess cash-management processes and risks, strengthen internal controls, identify opportunities for improvement, and implement or recommend measures that enhance efficiency, accountability, compliance and reliability.

dimensions.name: Cash Process and Control Assessment
dimensions.definition: Ability to review cash processes and assess whether controls, segregation of duties and procedures are operating as intended.

levels.Emerging: Applies prescribed control checks and reports observed weaknesses with guidance.
levels.Developing: Reviews routine processes for compliance with established controls and identifies basic gaps.
levels.Proficient: Assesses complex processes, evaluates control effectiveness and recommends corrective measures.
levels.Advanced: Leads division-level control reviews and strengthens systems for sustained control effectiveness.

dimensions.name: Risk and Compliance Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify operational, financial and compliance risks and recommend appropriate mitigating actions.

levels.Emerging: Identifies obvious operational or compliance risks and seeks guidance.
levels.Developing: Monitors assigned risks and applies established mitigating controls.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex risks and coordinates appropriate mitigation and escalation.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on significant cash-management risks and strengthens the division's risk-control framework.

dimensions.name: Process Improvement and Efficiency
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify bottlenecks, improve workflows and support measurable improvements in cash operations.

levels.Emerging: Suggests simple improvements to assigned processes with guidance.
levels.Developing: Implements approved improvements that enhance timeliness or reduce errors.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes process bottlenecks and develops practical improvements using evidence and operational data.
levels.Advanced: Leads continuous-improvement initiatives and institutionalizes efficient, reliable cash-management practices.

dimensions.name: Audit Observation and Corrective Action Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to respond to audit observations, identify root causes and monitor corrective actions.

levels.Emerging: Assists in gathering documents and implementing assigned corrective actions.
levels.Developing: Tracks routine audit observations and completes assigned corrective actions on time.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes root causes of recurring observations and coordinates sustainable corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on audit readiness and establishes mechanisms that minimize recurring observations.

dimensions.name: Control Leadership and Knowledge Transfer
dimensions.definition: Ability to guide personnel, institutionalize good practices and sustain improvements in cash-management controls.

levels.Emerging: Follows established controls and shares basic instructions when requested.
levels.Developing: Supports peers in applying established procedures and controls.
levels.Proficient: Provides technical guidance on complex controls and coaches less experienced staff.
levels.Advanced: Mentors personnel, institutionalizes good practices and leads control-enhancement initiatives across the Division.

name: General Services Division
sourceFile: General Services Division_Revised Competency Framework Initial Draft.docx

careerProgression.meaning: Demonstrates basic awareness and understanding of the competency. Performs tasks with close guidance and applies standard procedures in familiar situations.

Demonstrates working knowledge and applies the competency with some independence. Handles routine tasks and moderately complex situations using established procedures and seeks guidance when necessary.
Demonstrates strong and consistent application of the competency. Independently handles complex situations, exercises sound judgment, and may guide or support others in applying the competency.

Demonstrates mastery of the competency and applies it strategically across complex and changing situations. Provides direction, mentors others, drives improvements, and contributes to organizational policies, systems, or strategic outcomes.

competencies.name: Service Delivery
competencies.definition: Provides timely, responsive, reliable, and client-focused administrative and general support services that meet established standards and contribute to effective Department operations.

dimensions.name: Client Responsiveness
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand client needs, provide timely assistance, and communicate appropriate information or action.

levels.Emerging: Responds to routine requests with guidance and follows established service procedures.
levels.Developing: Handles routine client requests independently and provides clear, timely information.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex service concerns using sound judgment and adjusts service approaches to client needs.
levels.Advanced: Establishes service approaches and standards that improve client experience and organizational responsiveness.

dimensions.name: Service Quality and Reliability
dimensions.definition: Ability to deliver accurate, complete, consistent, and dependable services within agreed standards.

levels.Emerging: Performs assigned services according to established procedures and quality requirements.
levels.Developing: Consistently completes routine services accurately and within prescribed standards.
levels.Proficient: Monitors service quality, addresses recurring issues, and improves reliability of service delivery.
levels.Advanced: Drives division-wide service quality improvements and establishes mechanisms for sustained service excellence.

dimensions.name: Continuous Service Improvement
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify opportunities and implement practical improvements in service processes.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes simple opportunities to improve own work with guidance.
levels.Developing: Suggests and applies practical improvements to routine service processes.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes service gaps and implements improvements based on feedback and performance information.
levels.Advanced: Leads service innovation and institutionalizes improvements across functions or organizational units.

dimensions.name: Professional Accountability
dimensions.definition: Ability to demonstrate responsibility, transparency, responsiveness, and appropriate conduct in delivering services.

levels.Emerging: Completes assigned work and seeks guidance when issues arise.
levels.Developing: Takes ownership of routine deliverables and promptly escalates issues requiring higher-level action.
levels.Proficient: Exercises sound judgment and accountability in complex or urgent service situations.
levels.Advanced: Models accountability and establishes practices that strengthen organizational trust and service performance.

competencies.name: Administrative Support and Coordination
competencies.definition: Provides efficient administrative support by managing documents, coordinating tasks, facilitating communications, and handling matters pertinent to GSD functions and responsibilities.

dimensions.name: Administrative Documentation
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, organize, route, and monitor administrative documents accurately and efficiently.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine documents using prescribed formats with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently prepares and tracks routine administrative documents and submissions.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex documentation requirements and improves document workflows.
levels.Advanced: Establishes efficient administrative documentation systems and standards.

dimensions.name: Task and Workflow Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate multiple administrative tasks, schedules, dependencies, and follow-through requirements.

levels.Emerging: Tracks assigned tasks with close guidance.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine tasks and follows up on pending actions.
levels.Proficient: Manages competing priorities, dependencies, and urgent requirements across functions.
levels.Advanced: Optimizes workflows and establishes coordination mechanisms for division-wide efficiency.

dimensions.name: Internal Coordination and Communication
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate with offices, divisions, personnel, and service providers to facilitate timely completion of work.

levels.Emerging: Communicates routine matters using established channels.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine requests and clarifies requirements with concerned parties.
levels.Proficient: Facilitates complex or cross-functional coordination and resolves communication gaps.
levels.Advanced: Builds effective coordination systems and represents GSD in complex administrative matters.

dimensions.name: Administrative Problem Solving
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify administrative issues, determine appropriate actions, and escalate matters when necessary.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common administrative issues and seeks guidance.
levels.Developing: Resolves routine administrative problems using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex administrative issues and recommends practical solutions.
levels.Advanced: Provides direction on recurring administrative issues and drives systemic improvements.

competencies.name: Policy Implementation and Compliance
competencies.definition: Implements, monitors, and promotes compliance with applicable laws, policies, procedures, standards, and Department issuances relevant to General Services operations, and provides appropriate guidance on compliance matters.

dimensions.name: Policy Interpretation
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand and interpret applicable policies, procedures, standards, and Department issuances.

levels.Emerging: Identifies and follows policies applicable to assigned tasks with guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies relevant policies to routine situations and seeks clarification when necessary.
levels.Proficient: Interprets requirements in complex situations and provides sound operational guidance.
levels.Advanced: Provides authoritative technical guidance and contributes to policy clarification or development.

dimensions.name: Policy Implementation
dimensions.definition: Ability to translate policies and procedures into consistent operational practices.

levels.Emerging: Follows established procedures in familiar situations.
levels.Developing: Applies procedures consistently and supports implementation within assigned functions.
levels.Proficient: Adapts implementation approaches to complex operational requirements while maintaining compliance.
levels.Advanced: Leads implementation strategies and establishes systems that institutionalize policy requirements.

dimensions.name: Compliance Monitoring
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor adherence, identify gaps, and recommend corrective actions.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes obvious compliance issues and reports them.
levels.Developing: Performs routine compliance checks using established tools or criteria.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes compliance gaps and recommends or coordinates corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes compliance monitoring systems and advises management on systemic risks.

dimensions.name: Compliance Advisory and Improvement
dimensions.definition: Ability to provide guidance and improve procedures based on compliance findings and operational experience.

levels.Emerging: Seeks guidance when requirements are unclear.
levels.Developing: Provides basic clarification on routine requirements.
levels.Proficient: Provides practical guidance on complex compliance issues and recommends process improvements.
levels.Advanced: Shapes improved policies, controls, and practices based on compliance trends and organizational needs.

competencies.name: Facilities and Operational Risk Management
competencies.definition: Manages workplace facilities and operational risks by identifying hazards, assessing potential impacts, coordinating preventive actions, and supporting safe, reliable, and continuous operations, excluding functions assigned to the Asset Management Division.

dimensions.name: Risk Identification
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify hazards, vulnerabilities, and conditions that may affect facilities or operations.

levels.Emerging: Identifies obvious hazards or operational risks using established checklists and guidance.
levels.Developing: Identifies common operational and facility risks and documents them using established methods.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes multiple risk sources and identifies risks affecting operations, projects, or service continuity.
levels.Advanced: Anticipates emerging risks and establishes systematic approaches for organization-wide risk identification.

dimensions.name: Risk Assessment and Evaluation
dimensions.definition: Ability to determine the likelihood, impact, and significance of identified risks.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic risk consequences with guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies established approaches to assess routine risks and determine appropriate priorities.
levels.Proficient: Uses various approaches to determine, understand, and evaluate risks, particularly for complex operations.
levels.Advanced: Leads risk assessment approaches and advises management on significant operational and facility risks.

dimensions.name: Risk Mitigation and Controls
dimensions.definition: Ability to formulate and coordinate preventive, corrective, and contingency measures.

levels.Emerging: Recommends basic control measures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Implements established preventive and corrective actions for identified risks.
levels.Proficient: Develops practical mitigation and contingency measures and coordinates their implementation.
levels.Advanced: Designs integrated risk-control strategies and drives sustained risk reduction.

dimensions.name: Operational Continuity
dimensions.definition: Ability to support continuity of essential services during disruptions, emergencies, or changing operating conditions.

levels.Emerging: Follows established contingency procedures during routine disruptions.
levels.Developing: Coordinates assigned continuity actions and escalates issues appropriately.
levels.Proficient: Assesses operational impacts and recommends continuity measures for complex disruptions.
levels.Advanced: Leads continuity planning improvements and advises management on resilience and preparedness.

competencies.name: Maintenance and Support Services Management
competencies.definition: Plans, coordinates, monitors, and improves office support services such as upkeep, janitorial, security, reproduction, telecommunications, and related administrative support services to ensure efficient and reliable operations.

dimensions.name: Support Service Planning
dimensions.definition: Ability to determine service requirements, priorities, schedules, and resources for office support functions.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine support requirements with guidance.
levels.Developing: Plans routine support activities using established schedules and service requirements.
levels.Proficient: Integrates service requirements across functions and adjusts plans to operational needs.
levels.Advanced: Establishes service strategies and resource approaches for sustained support operations.

dimensions.name: Service Operations Monitoring
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor delivery, quality, timeliness, and responsiveness of support services.

levels.Emerging: Checks completion of assigned support activities using basic standards.
levels.Developing: Monitors routine service delivery and reports issues promptly.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes service performance and implements corrective actions for recurring issues.
levels.Advanced: Establishes performance monitoring systems and drives continuous improvement in support services.

dimensions.name: Service Provider Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate with internal and external service providers to ensure agreed service requirements are met.

levels.Emerging: Coordinates routine requests with guidance.
levels.Developing: Communicates requirements and follows up on routine provider commitments.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex provider coordination and resolves service performance issues.
levels.Advanced: Leads service-provider governance and establishes mechanisms for sustained service quality.

dimensions.name: Resource and Service Continuity
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain availability of essential support services and respond to disruptions.

levels.Emerging: Follows established procedures during service interruptions.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine corrective actions and escalates significant disruptions.
levels.Proficient: Develops contingency measures and coordinates continuity of critical support services.
levels.Advanced: Leads resilience and continuity improvements for essential administrative support functions.

competencies.name: Government Procurement Management
competencies.definition: Plans, prepares, coordinates, reviews, and monitors procurement requirements and related documentation in accordance with applicable government procurement laws, rules, regulations, and Department procedures.

dimensions.name: Procurement Planning
dimensions.definition: Ability to translate operational requirements into accurate and timely procurement plans and requests.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine procurement requirements using established plans, forms, and guidance.
levels.Developing: Prepares routine procurement requirements and supports PPMP, Supplemental PPMP, and related planning activities.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes operational requirements, timing, priorities, and procurement approaches for complex requirements.
levels.Advanced: Provides strategic procurement-planning guidance and improves approaches for timely, compliant, and cost-effective procurement.

dimensions.name: Procurement Documentation
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, verify, and maintain complete procurement-related documents.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine procurement documents using prescribed formats with guidance.
levels.Developing: Reviews routine PRs, APRs, and supporting documents for completeness and compliance.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex documentation deficiencies and ensures procurement submissions meet applicable requirements.
levels.Advanced: Establishes document-quality controls and standards that improve procurement efficiency and compliance.

dimensions.name: Procurement Process Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate procurement requirements and actions with concerned offices, suppliers, and the Head of Procuring Entity or authorized procurement bodies.

levels.Emerging: Coordinates assigned procurement requirements with guidance.
levels.Developing: Follows up routine procurement actions and clarifies requirements with concerned parties.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex coordination issues, timelines, and dependencies across procurement activities.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens procurement coordination mechanisms and advises on process improvements.

dimensions.name: Procurement Compliance and Risk Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify procurement risks and ensure adherence to applicable procurement requirements.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic procurement requirements and escalates uncertainties.
levels.Developing: Applies established procurement rules and controls to routine transactions.
levels.Proficient: Identifies compliance gaps and recommends corrective actions for complex procurement requirements.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert guidance on procurement risks and contributes to stronger procurement controls and systems.

competencies.name: Supply Chain, Inventory and Materials Management
competencies.definition: Plans, coordinates, monitors, and improves the acquisition, availability, inspection, acceptance, storage, issuance, movement, utilization, reconciliation, and accountability of supplies and materials supporting GSD operations.

dimensions.name: Supply Planning and Forecasting
dimensions.definition: Ability to determine supply requirements based on operational needs, usage patterns, priorities, and available resources.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine supply requirements using established information and guidance.
levels.Developing: Prepares supply requirements and forecasts for routine operations using established methods.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes demand patterns and develops supply plans for complex or changing operational needs.
levels.Advanced: Establishes strategic supply-planning approaches and aligns supply resources with organizational priorities.

dimensions.name: Inventory and Materials Control
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain accurate information on supplies and materials and monitor their availability, movement, storage, and utilization.

levels.Emerging: Performs basic inventory and materials tasks with guidance.
levels.Developing: Maintains accurate supply information and coordinates routine movement, storage, and replenishment.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes inventory issues and improves availability, utilization, and control of materials.
levels.Advanced: Establishes integrated inventory and materials controls and drives system improvements.

dimensions.name: Inspection, Acceptance and Issuance
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate inspection and acceptance of delivered supplies and control their authorized issuance.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing or routing routine inspection, acceptance, and issuance documents with guidance.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine RFI, IAR, and RIS requirements and checks supporting documents.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex inspection, acceptance, issuance, and documentation issues and coordinates corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Establishes effective controls for inspection, acceptance, issuance, and service readiness.

dimensions.name: Inventory Reconciliation and Accountability
dimensions.definition: Ability to reconcile inventory records, monitor balances and issuances, and support physical inventory accountability.

levels.Emerging: Records routine inventory transactions and reports discrepancies with guidance.
levels.Developing: Prepares or supports routine RSMI, PS-LR/MSPIB, and inventory records using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes inventory variances, supports physical counts, reconciles records, and recommends corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens inventory accountability systems and uses inventory information to improve resource stewardship and decision-making.

dimensions.name: Supply Chain Risk Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify and mitigate risks affecting supply availability, quality, cost, accountability, and continuity.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common supply risks and escalates concerns.
levels.Developing: Applies established controls to address routine supply risks.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes supply risks and develops mitigation or contingency measures.
levels.Advanced: Leads supply resilience strategies and advises management on significant supply-chain risks.

competencies.name: Financial Transactions and Disbursement Management
competencies.definition: Processes, reviews, verifies, monitors, and manages financial transactions, disbursements, cash advances, liquidations, and related supporting documents accurately, timely, transparently, and in accordance with applicable government financial management requirements.

dimensions.name: Financial Transaction Processing
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, verify, process, and monitor bills, payment documents, and related financial transactions.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine financial forms and supporting documents with close guidance.
levels.Developing: Processes routine bills and payment transactions using established procedures and checks completeness.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex transactions, resolves documentation issues, and coordinates required actions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes efficient transaction-processing approaches and provides direction on complex cases.

dimensions.name: Disbursement and Payment Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to review and ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance of disbursement and payment documents.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic payment and disbursement requirements and follows prescribed procedures.
levels.Developing: Reviews routine payment documents for completeness and compliance before endorsement.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex payment issues and coordinates resolution of deficiencies.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical guidance and improves disbursement controls and processing systems.

dimensions.name: Cash Advance and Liquidation Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to review, process, monitor, and reconcile cash advances and liquidation documents in accordance with applicable requirements.

levels.Emerging: Prepares or checks routine cash advance and liquidation documents with guidance.
levels.Developing: Reviews routine cash advance and liquidation documents for completeness and timely submission.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex deficiencies, monitors outstanding accountabilities, and recommends appropriate corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens controls for cash advances and liquidation and advises management on recurring accountability risks.

dimensions.name: Financial Compliance and Internal Controls

levels.Proficient: Interprets requirements in complex transactions, analyzes discrepancies, and implements or recommends corrective controls.
levels.Advanced: Advises on financial compliance and contributes to stronger policies, controls, and procedures.

dimensions.name: Reconciliation and Financial Records
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain accurate financial records and reconcile transactions to support reliable reporting and accountability.

levels.Emerging: Maintains assigned financial records accurately with guidance.
levels.Developing: Updates records and performs routine reconciliation using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes discrepancies, completes complex reconciliation, and recommends corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens systems and controls for reliable financial records and reporting.

competencies.name: Fleet Management
competencies.definition: Coordinates and monitors the safe, reliable, compliant, and efficient operation, maintenance, registration, insurance, and utilization of service motor vehicles assigned for official Department operations.

dimensions.name: Fleet Operations
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate vehicle scheduling, utilization, availability, and operational requirements.

levels.Emerging: Supports routine vehicle scheduling and utilization monitoring with guidance.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine fleet requirements and maintains accurate operational information.
levels.Proficient: Optimizes vehicle utilization and resolves complex operational scheduling issues.
levels.Advanced: Establishes fleet utilization strategies and systems aligned with organizational requirements.

dimensions.name: Vehicle Maintenance and Reliability
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor preventive maintenance, repairs, roadworthiness, and service availability.

levels.Emerging: Follows established maintenance schedules and reports vehicle issues.
levels.Developing: Monitors routine maintenance and coordinates repairs using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes recurring maintenance issues and recommends actions to improve reliability.
levels.Advanced: Establishes fleet reliability strategies and drives preventive-maintenance improvements.

dimensions.name: Registration, Insurance and Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to ensure required documentation, registration, insurance, safety, and regulatory requirements are maintained.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic registration and insurance requirements with guidance.
levels.Developing: Monitors routine compliance requirements and maintains supporting records.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex compliance issues and coordinates timely corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes controls that ensure sustained fleet compliance and risk reduction.

dimensions.name: Fleet Safety and Risk Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify and manage risks associated with vehicle operations and official use.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common vehicle-operation risks and reports them.
levels.Developing: Applies established safety and risk-control measures.
levels.Proficient: Assesses fleet risks and recommends preventive or corrective measures.
levels.Advanced: Leads fleet safety and risk-management improvements and advises management on fleet resilience.

competencies.name: Building Maintenance and Repair
competencies.definition: Coordinates, monitors, and improves preventive maintenance, repair, inspection, and related building-service activities to maintain safe, functional, and reliable Department facilities.

dimensions.definition: Ability to plan and schedule preventive maintenance based on facility needs, service requirements, and risk.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine maintenance requirements with guidance.
levels.Developing: Implements established preventive-maintenance schedules and monitors completion.
levels.Proficient: Develops maintenance plans based on facility condition, usage, and risk information.
levels.Advanced: Establishes integrated preventive-maintenance strategies and prioritization approaches.

dimensions.name: Repair and Corrective Action
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate timely response to facility defects, breakdowns, and repair requirements.

levels.Emerging: Reports defects and follows established repair procedures.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine repair requests and monitors completion.
levels.Proficient: Prioritizes complex repair requirements and coordinates corrective actions with appropriate providers.
levels.Advanced: Leads systematic repair and corrective-maintenance improvements.

dimensions.name: Inspection and Condition Monitoring
dimensions.definition: Ability to inspect facilities, identify deficiencies, and assess conditions affecting safety and functionality.

levels.Emerging: Identifies obvious defects during routine checks with guidance.
levels.Developing: Conducts routine inspections using established standards and documents findings.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes inspection results and recommends appropriate corrective or preventive actions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes condition-monitoring approaches and advises management on facility priorities.

dimensions.name: Contractor and Service Provider Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate technical and maintenance service providers and monitor delivery against requirements.

levels.Emerging: Assists in routine coordination with guidance.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine provider activities and follows up on deliverables.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex provider coordination and addresses performance issues.
levels.Advanced: Establishes service-provider performance mechanisms and drives quality improvements.

name: Human Resource Development Division
basis: Basis: CY 2026 Division Performance Commitment and Review (DPCR) & Competency Validation Report

careerProgression.meaning: Performs routine assigned tasks using established procedures, formats, and controls; requires regular guidance.

competencies.name: Learning and Development Planning
competencies.definition: The ability to assess organizational, functional, and individual competency requirements; identify learning and development needs through competency assessment, performance results, and other diagnostic tools; and formulate, prioritize, schedule, and monitor competency-based learning and development interventions — including local training programs and local and foreign study and non-study grants — that align with organizational goals, strategic priorities, and workforce development requirements. This includes managing the Learning and Development Plan, Competency-Based Learning and Development Interventions (CBLDIs), Learning Calendars, local and foreign study and non-study grant pipelines, and evaluation mechanisms necessary to strengthen workforce capability.

dimensions.name: Learning Needs Analysis
dimensions.definition: Identifies competency, performance, and development gaps through data gathering, assessments, consultations, and other validated sources.

levels.Emerging: Gathers and consolidates learning needs data from various sources.
levels.Developing: Assists in validating learning and competency gaps using assessment results.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes learning needs data and identifies priority competency gaps.
levels.Advanced: Establishes enterprise-wide approaches and standards for learning needs analysis.

dimensions.name: Competency-Based Planning
dimensions.definition: Develops interventions and development initiatives — including training programs and study or non-study grants — based on validated competency gaps and organizational requirements.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing learning intervention recommendations.
levels.Developing: Develops proposed interventions based on identified competency gaps.
levels.Proficient: Reviews and prioritizes competency-based interventions aligned with organizational priorities.
levels.Advanced: Approves and strategically directs competency-based learning interventions across the organization.

dimensions.name: Learning Portfolio Management
dimensions.definition: Plans, prioritizes, schedules, and manages learning interventions and development programs, including L&D Plans, CBLDIs, Learning Calendars, and local and foreign study and non-study grant pipelines.

levels.Developing: Assists in preparing learning calendars and development plans.
levels.Proficient: Develops and manages annual L&D Plans, CBLDIs, and Learning Calendars.
levels.Advanced: Sets strategic directions and investment priorities for organizational learning portfolios.

dimensions.name: Monitoring and Alignment
dimensions.definition: Ensures learning plans remain aligned with organizational priorities, workforce requirements, and strategic goals.

levels.Emerging: Tracks status of learning interventions and learning plans.
levels.Developing: Monitors implementation progress and compliance with approved plans.
levels.Proficient: Evaluates alignment of interventions with competencies and organizational priorities.
levels.Advanced: Leads policy and strategic decisions to ensure organizational alignment of learning investments.

dimensions.name: Learning and Development Processing
dimensions.definition: Manages the evaluation, screening, validation, and endorsement of applications for local and foreign study and non-study grants.

levels.Emerging: Assists in receiving, organizing, and validating learning and development application documents.
levels.Developing: Screens applications and verifies compliance with qualification requirements.
levels.Proficient: Reviews and evaluates learning and development applications and endorses qualified applicants.
levels.Advanced: Establishes policies, standards, and systems governing learning and development administration and selection processes.

competencies.name: Program/Course Design and Development
competencies.definition: The ability to systematically design, develop, review, and improve learning interventions, courses, competency development programs, and capability-building initiatives using instructional design principles, adult learning methodologies, competency standards, and organizational requirements. This includes preparing training designs, curricula, learning activity plans, session guides, syllabi, instructional materials, digital learning resources, participant guides, facilitator guides, evaluation mechanisms, and budgetary requirements for both local and foreign learning opportunities.

dimensions.name: Instructional Design
dimensions.definition: Designs learning solutions using instructional systems design principles and adult learning methodologies.

levels.Emerging: Assists in developing learning objectives and session outlines.
levels.Developing: Develops learning objectives and activity plans for assigned programs.
levels.Proficient: Designs comprehensive learning interventions using instructional design standards.
levels.Advanced: Establishes organizational standards and frameworks for instructional design.

dimensions.name: Learning Content Development
dimensions.definition: Develops learning materials, guides, manuals, and digital learning resources.

levels.Emerging: Prepares basic learning materials and presentation slides.
levels.Developing: Develops learning materials based on approved content requirements.
levels.Proficient: Produces participant manuals, facilitator guides, and instructional resources.
levels.Advanced: Directs development and innovation of organization-wide learning content systems.

dimensions.name: Program Development
dimensions.definition: Designs complete learning programs, interventions, and development initiatives aligned with learning objectives.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing learning program components and documentation.
levels.Developing: Develops program structures, methodologies, and schedules.
levels.Proficient: Designs integrated capability-building and competency-development programs.
levels.Advanced: Leads development of strategic organizational learning programs and learning architectures.

dimensions.name: Quality Assurance and Review
dimensions.definition: Reviews and validates learning designs, materials, and programs to ensure relevance, quality, and compliance.

levels.Emerging: Assists in checking learning materials for completeness and consistency.
levels.Developing: Reviews learning materials against established standards.
levels.Proficient: Evaluates and recommends improvements to learning designs and programs.
levels.Advanced: Approves quality standards and drives continuous improvement of learning design systems.

competencies.name: Program/Course Delivery and Administration
competencies.definition: The ability to effectively manage, coordinate, administer, facilitate, and monitor learning and development programs, capability-building initiatives, and other developmental interventions. This includes managing the logistical, operational, financial, administrative, and documentation requirements necessary to ensure successful implementation and compliance with organizational policies and standards.

dimensions.name: Program Administration
dimensions.definition: Manages participant registration, communications, documentation, and overall training administration activities.

levels.Emerging: Assists in participant registration, documentation, and communication activities.
levels.Developing: Coordinates participant requirements and learning administration processes.
levels.Proficient: Manages end-to-end administration of assigned learning programs.
levels.Advanced: Establishes and improves systems governing learning administration across the organization.

dimensions.name: Logistics and Resource Management
dimensions.definition: Ensures availability and management of venues, facilities, equipment, materials, and other required resources.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing learning materials, venues, and equipment.
levels.Developing: Coordinates logistical requirements and resource availability for learning activities.
levels.Proficient: Manages allocation and utilization of resources to support learning interventions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes policies and resource strategies supporting organizational learning operations.

dimensions.name: Learning Operations Management

levels.Emerging: Supports implementation of scheduled learning activities.
levels.Developing: Coordinates learning schedules, participants, and delivery arrangements.
levels.Proficient: Oversees implementation and operational execution of learning programs.
levels.Advanced: Directs organizational learning operations and resolves complex implementation issues.

dimensions.name: Financial and Administrative Support

levels.Proficient: Reviews budgetary, documentary, and compliance requirements for learning programs.
levels.Advanced: Approves resource allocation strategies and administrative controls supporting learning operations.

dimensions.name: Resource Allocation

levels.Developing: Coordinates resource requirements and monitors utilization of facilities, equipment, supplies, and financial resources for assigned programs.
levels.Proficient: Reviews resource utilization and recommends adjustments to ensure efficient implementation of learning interventions.
levels.Advanced: Develops resource allocation strategies, establishes allocation standards, and optimizes organizational resources to support learning and development programs.

dimensions.name: Learning and Development Coordination
dimensions.definition: Facilitates communication and coordination among applicants, development partners, oversight bodies, and internal stakeholders for local and foreign study and non-study grants.

levels.Emerging: Assists in disseminating learning and development opportunities and communicating requirements.
levels.Developing: Coordinates with applicants, offices, and development partners regarding learning and development processes.
levels.Proficient: Manages stakeholder coordination and resolves process-related concerns.
levels.Advanced: Leads strategic partnerships and institutional learning and development initiatives.

competencies.name: Learning Facilitation

levels.Emerging: Assists facilitators in conducting learning activities and administering learning sessions.
levels.Developing: Conducts assigned portions of learning activities using prescribed methodologies.
levels.Proficient: Facilitates complete learning sessions and adapts facilitation techniques to participant needs.
levels.Advanced: Leads complex learning interventions and establishes facilitation standards and methodologies.

dimensions.name: Learner Engagement
dimensions.definition: Creates opportunities for active participation, interaction, and learner involvement throughout the learning process.

levels.Emerging: Supports participant participation and addresses routine learner concerns.
levels.Developing: Applies engagement methods to encourage interaction and participation.
levels.Proficient: Utilizes varied learning approaches and technologies to sustain learner engagement.
levels.Advanced: Designs innovative engagement strategies and mentors facilitators in learner-centered approaches.

dimensions.name: Learning Environment Management

levels.Emerging: Assists in maintaining conducive learning conditions and managing participant concerns.

levels.Proficient: Handles complex learning situations and promotes inclusive learning environments.
levels.Advanced: Establishes standards and strategies for managing diverse and high-impact learning environments.

dimensions.name: Learning Integration
dimensions.definition: Reinforces learning by facilitating reflection, synthesis, application, and transfer of learning to the workplace.

levels.Emerging: Assists in documenting learning outputs and participant reflections.
levels.Developing: Facilitates learning synthesis and reflection activities.
levels.Proficient: Guides participants in applying learned concepts to workplace situations.
levels.Advanced: Promotes organizational learning and institutionalizes learning transfer mechanisms.

competencies.name: Learning Measurement and Evaluation

levels.Proficient: Performs comprehensive analysis to determine effectiveness and competency gaps.
levels.Advanced: Generates strategic insights and recommendations for organizational capability development.

dimensions.definition: Develops reports, recommendations, and action plans based on evaluation findings, and maintains records, databases, and status reports for local and foreign study and non-study grants, in compliance with applicable policies and reportorial requirements.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing evaluation summaries, reports, and study and non-study grant status records.
levels.Developing: Prepares evaluation reports and presents findings, including study and non-study grant status and compliance reports.
levels.Proficient: Develops recommendations and improvement plans based on learning outcomes, and ensures study and non-study grant reports comply with applicable policies and requirements.
levels.Advanced: Uses evaluation findings to influence organizational learning strategies and policy decisions, and directs study and non-study grant reporting and compliance systems.

competencies.name: Competency Development and Validation
