competencies.definition: The ability to systematically manage, maintain, organize, secure, retrieve, archive, and report human resource development records, databases, information repositories, and knowledge resources in compliance with records management standards, data privacy requirements, and regulatory guidelines. This includes ensuring the accuracy, integrity, accessibility, retention, disposition, and reporting of HRDD records and information resources to support operational efficiency, decision-making, organizational accountability, and institutional memory

dimensions.name: Records Administration
dimensions.definition: Manages the creation, filing, maintenance, organization, retrieval, and disposal of physical and electronic records in accordance with established standards and procedures.

levels.Emerging: Files, organizes, and maintains physical and electronic records according to prescribed procedures and filing systems.
levels.Developing: Manages records requests, retrieval activities, and routine updates of records and files.
levels.Proficient: Reviews records management practices and recommends improvements to filing, retrieval, and maintenance processes.
levels.Advanced: Develops and implements organization-wide records management standards, systems, and process improvements.

dimensions.name: Database Management
dimensions.definition: Maintains the accuracy, completeness, integrity, and accessibility of HRDD databases, information systems, and data repositories.

levels.Emerging: Encodes, updates, and maintains information in HRDD databases and tracking systems.
levels.Developing: Validates database entries and ensures completeness and accuracy of records and information.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes database information, resolves data integrity issues, and recommends enhancements to database processes.
levels.Advanced: Leads the development and governance of records and database management systems to improve organizational efficiency and decision-making.

dimensions.name: Archives and Document Control
dimensions.definition: Administers archiving, records retention, inventory, document tracking, retrieval, and transmittal processes in compliance with applicable regulations.

levels.Emerging: Assists in records inventory, document tracking, archiving, and retrieval activities.
levels.Developing: Maintains records retention schedules and prepares records for archiving, transfer, or disposal.
levels.Proficient: Reviews compliance with archival requirements and document control procedures and recommends improvements.
levels.Advanced: Establishes archiving, retention, disposition, and document control strategies aligned with institutional and regulatory requirements.

dimensions.name: Information Governance and Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ensures compliance with records management policies, data privacy requirements, reporting standards, retention schedules, and information quality management practices.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing records-related reports and ensuring proper handling of information.
levels.Developing: Monitors compliance with records management policies, reporting requirements, and data privacy standards.
levels.Proficient: Reviews reports for accuracy, completeness, and compliance, and recommends corrective measures when necessary.
levels.Advanced: Leads information governance initiatives, establishes reporting standards, and ensures organizational compliance with records management and data governance requirements.

dimensions.name: Monitoring and Reporting
dimensions.definition: Tracks records management activities, database status, compliance requirements, and reportorial obligations to ensure timely submission of accurate information and management reports.

levels.Emerging: Compiles records and database information for monitoring and reporting purposes.
levels.Developing: Monitors record status, reporting deadlines, and submission requirements and prepares routine reports.
levels.Proficient: Reviews records management reports, analyzes trends, and recommends improvements to reporting processes and information quality.
levels.Advanced: Develops organizational monitoring and reporting systems that support decision-making, compliance, and strategic information management.

competencies.name: Audio-Visual and Conference Systems Management
competencies.definition: The ability to set up, operate, maintain, and troubleshoot audio-visual equipment, conferencing systems, and related facilities technology to support training programs, meetings, and department events, ensuring reliable and effective use of conference rooms and multimedia resources.

dimensions.name: Equipment Setup and Operation
dimensions.definition: Sets up and operates audio-visual equipment, conferencing systems, and related facilities technology for programs, meetings, and events.

levels.Emerging: Assists in setting up basic audio-visual equipment following established procedures.
levels.Developing: Independently sets up and operates standard audio-visual and conferencing equipment for routine programs and meetings.
levels.Proficient: Configures and operates complex audio-visual and conferencing setups for high-profile programs and events.
levels.Advanced: Establishes standards and best practices for audio-visual equipment setup and operation across the Department.

dimensions.name: Troubleshooting and Technical Support
dimensions.definition: Diagnoses and resolves audio-visual and conference room technical issues to ensure uninterrupted service.

levels.Emerging: Reports technical issues and seeks guidance in resolving basic equipment problems.
levels.Developing: Diagnoses and resolves common audio-visual and conferencing issues with minimal supervision.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex technical issues during live programs and events, minimizing disruption.
levels.Advanced: Leads resolution of critical technical failures and develops contingency protocols for audio-visual operations.

dimensions.name: Preventive Maintenance
dimensions.definition: Inspects, maintains, and coordinates repair of audio-visual equipment and conference room systems to ensure functionality and longevity.

levels.Emerging: Assists in routine inspection and cleaning of audio-visual equipment.
levels.Developing: Conducts regular preventive maintenance checks and logs equipment condition.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates repair and servicing of equipment and recommends upgrades or replacements.
levels.Advanced: Establishes a preventive maintenance program and equipment lifecycle standards for conference room systems.

dimensions.name: Conference Room and Facilities Coordination
dimensions.definition: Manages conference room scheduling, equipment readiness, and coordination with users to support programs, meetings, and events.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing conference rooms and checking equipment readiness before scheduled use.
levels.Developing: Coordinates conference room scheduling and equipment readiness with requesting offices.
levels.Proficient: Manages competing scheduling requirements and resolves conference room and equipment conflicts.
levels.Advanced: Establishes conference room and facilities-technology management policies and standards for the Department.

competencies.name: Recruitment, Selection, and Placement
competencies.definition: The ability to establish, enhance, and execute fair, competency-based, and policy-compliant recruitment, selection, and placement systems and practices to support the Department’s workforce requirements and strategic goals.

dimensions.name: RSP Policy and Governance
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand, apply, review, and improve Recruitment, Selection, and Placement (RSP) policies, guidelines, and processes within applicable Civil Service Commission (CSC), Department of Budget and Management (DBM), and Department requirements.

levels.Emerging: Refers to applicable RSP policies and follows established procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies RSP policies to routine transactions and identifies when clarification is needed.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex RSP issues, interprets requirements, and recommends process improvements.
levels.Advanced: Leads proactive review and enhancement of RSP policies/processes in response to strategic workforce needs.

dimensions.name: Workforce and Recruitment Planning
dimensions.definition: Ability to translate approved staffing requirements, vacancies, and workforce information into recruitment plans, sourcing activities, and placement actions.

levels.Emerging: Uses approved staffing information to support routine vacancy-filling activities with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently prepares routine recruitment schedules/plans for approved vacancies.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes workforce and vacancy information to improve recruitment priorities and approaches.
levels.Advanced: Leads strategic staffing and recruitment planning that supports medium-and long-term workforce needs.

dimensions.name: Talent Sourcing and Attraction
dimensions.definition: Ability to use appropriate internal and external recruitment channels and approaches to attract qualified and diverse applicants.

levels.Emerging: Assists in posting vacancies and using prescribed recruitment channels.
levels.Developing: Independently uses appropriate internal/external sourcing channels for routine vacancies.
levels.Proficient: Evaluates sourcing effectiveness and develops targeted approaches for difficult or specialized vacancies.
levels.Advanced: Leads proactive talent-attraction strategies, talent pooling, or employer-branding initiatives within assigned authority.

dimensions.name: Selection, Assessment, and Placement
dimensions.definition: Ability to evaluate applicants against qualification standards, job requirements, and competency criteria and provide technical/secretariat support to the Personnel Selection Board (PSB) and appointing authority.

levels.Emerging: Applies qualification standards and prescribed selection procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently screens applicants and supports routine assessment, PSB documentation, and placement requirements.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex candidate assessment and provides sound technical advice to PSB/hiring managers.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on competency-based selection systems, assessment methods, and placement processes.

dimensions.name: Equal Employment Opportunity and Onboarding
dimensions.definition: Ability to apply fair and inclusive selection principles and facilitate onboarding and placement activities that support adjustment, role understanding, and organizational integration.

levels.Emerging: Applies prescribed fair-selection and onboarding requirements with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently coordinates routine inclusive recruitment, placement, and orientation activities.
levels.Proficient: Reviews selection/onboarding practices and recommends improvements for fairness, accessibility, and employee adjustment.
levels.Advanced: Leads integrated, fair, and inclusive RSP/onboarding improvements aligned with workforce strategy.

competencies.name: Compensation and Benefits Management
competencies.definition: The ability to administer, review, and improve compensation and benefits systems and services in accordance with applicable policies, rules, and regulations while promoting accuracy, equity, timeliness, and responsive employee service.

dimensions.name: Compensation and Benefits Policy Application
dimensions.definition: Ability to interpret and apply applicable compensation, benefits, salary, and entitlement policies, rules, issuances, and standards.

levels.Emerging: Identifies applicable requirements and performs routine processing with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently applies established policies to routine compensation and benefits transactions.
levels.Proficient: Interprets complex requirements and provides sound technical guidance on difficult cases.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on complex compensation/benefits issues and contributes to improved policy or system implementation.

dimensions.name: Compensation and Benefits Administration
dimensions.definition: Ability to process, validate, and coordinate salaries, adjustments, benefits, entitlements, and related employee transactions.

levels.Emerging: Assists in processing routine salary, adjustment, benefit, and entitlement transactions.
levels.Developing: Independently processes routine transactions and coordinates deficiencies or clarifications.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex compensation/benefits cases and coordinates corrective action across concerned offices.
levels.Advanced: Improves controls and service mechanisms for high-volume or high-impact compensation and benefits processes.

dimensions.name: Benefits Advisory and Employee Assistance
dimensions.definition: Ability to provide accurate information and appropriate assistance to employees regarding benefits, entitlements, and compensation-related concerns.

levels.Emerging: Provides basic information using approved references with guidance.
levels.Developing: Responds independently to routine employee benefit and compensation queries.
levels.Proficient: Provides accurate guidance on complex employee concerns and identifies appropriate escalation or resolution paths.
levels.Advanced: Establishes or improves employee-assistance approaches that strengthen consistency, accessibility, and service quality.

dimensions.name: Compensation Analysis and Equity
dimensions.definition: Ability to analyze compensation and benefits information and provide technical inputs regarding internal/external equity and management decisions.

levels.Emerging: Organizes compensation information and identifies obvious discrepancies with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently prepares routine compensation information and technical inputs.
levels.Proficient: Conducts more complex analysis and develops evidence-based recommendations on equity or emerging issues.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert analytical support for compensation policy, planning, and system improvements.

dimensions.name: Compliance, Reporting, and Records
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain accurate supporting records and prepare timely compensation and benefits reports, submissions, and documentary requirements.

levels.Emerging: Maintains routine records and prepares required reports with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently completes routine reports and maintains supporting evidence.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex reports, validates data, and resolves material discrepancies.
levels.Advanced: Establishes stronger compliance/reporting controls and improves information reliability for management decisions.

competencies.name: Employee Relations, Welfare, Discipline, and Succession Planning
competencies.definition: The ability to establish and execute employee-relations practices that promote a fair, respectful, and supportive workplace through employee welfare, conflict management, discipline, engagement, succession, and employee-lifecycle support.

dimensions.name: Employee Relations and Workplace Concerns
dimensions.definition: Ability to address employee concerns, grievances, and workplace-relations matters using fair and appropriate HR processes.

levels.Emerging: Applies established employee-relations procedures with close guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently handles routine employee concerns and refers complex matters appropriately.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex employee-relations concerns using sound judgment and provides technical guidance.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on sensitive employee-relations matters and improves employee-relations systems.

dimensions.name: Conflict Management and Dispute Resolution
dimensions.definition: Ability to prevent, manage, and resolve workplace conflicts and disputes through structured, impartial, and constructive approaches.

levels.Emerging: Uses prescribed approaches to document and refer routine conflicts with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently supports routine conflict resolution and facilitates appropriate coordination.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex disputes using impartial analysis and appropriate intervention strategies.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on sensitive disputes and strengthens conflict-management mechanisms.

dimensions.name: Employee Welfare and Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to implement employee-welfare, incentive, and workplace-support policies and services.

levels.Emerging: Implements welfare and support policies with close supervision.
levels.Developing: Independently implements routine welfare, incentive, and employee-support procedures.
levels.Proficient: Guides others on complex welfare concerns and recommends targeted improvements.
levels.Advanced: Oversees welfare implementation, makes informed decisions, and introduces service enhancements.

dimensions.name: Employee Discipline and Administrative Action
dimensions.definition: Ability to apply and coordinate procedures on employee conduct, decorum, investigation, and administrative action within assigned authority.

levels.Emerging: Applies conduct, decorum, and administrative procedures with close supervision.
levels.Developing: Independently applies prescribed procedures to routine discipline matters.
levels.Proficient: Handles complex investigation/process issues and guides others on proper procedures.
levels.Advanced: Oversees complex discipline processes, provides expert direction, and strengthens procedural controls.

dimensions.name: Succession, Engagement, and Employee Lifecycle Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to support succession, engagement, retention, and employee-lifecycle activities within the Human Resource Management Division's (HRMD) assigned scope.

levels.Emerging: Supports assigned succession, engagement, or employee-lifecycle activities using established procedures.
levels.Developing: Independently coordinates routine lifecycle, engagement, and succession requirements.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes workforce/employee information and recommends targeted engagement, retention, or succession measures.
levels.Advanced: Provides strategic direction on assigned succession/lifecycle systems and organizational continuity improvements.

competencies.name: Rewards and Recognition Management
competencies.definition: The ability to plan, implement, monitor, and improve rewards and recognition programs that fairly recognize employee performance, innovation, exemplary behavior, and service in accordance with applicable policies and organizational goals.

dimensions.name: R&R Policy and Governance
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand, review, and improve rewards and recognition policies, guidelines, and processes.

levels.Emerging: Refers to applicable R&R policies and guidelines in performing assigned activities.
levels.Developing: Reviews routine R&R processes and refines them to meet agency requirements.
levels.Proficient: Develops customized R&R policies/processes linked with other HR systems.
levels.Advanced: Leads proactive review and updating of R&R policies and processes to respond to strategic changes.

dimensions.name: R&R Planning and Program Development
dimensions.definition: Ability to plan and develop R&R programs aligned with policy requirements, organizational needs, and available resources.

levels.Emerging: Maintains and updates information on applicable R&R programs with guidance.
levels.Developing: Develops routine annual R&R activities and coordinates required resources.
levels.Proficient: Develops integrated R&R plans linked to other HR systems and organizational needs.
levels.Advanced: Develops long-term R&R strategies aligned with organizational plans and strategic objectives.

dimensions.name: R&R Screening and Selection
dimensions.definition: Ability to apply fair, objective, and documented criteria and processes in identifying and selecting awardees.

levels.Emerging: Maintains records and follows prescribed screening and selection criteria.
levels.Developing: Collaborates with the R&R Committee in applying routine criteria/processes.
levels.Proficient: Develops criteria that consider relevant HR and stakeholder inputs and evidence.
levels.Advanced: Leads proactive review of criteria/processes to ensure fairness, consistency, and objectivity.

dimensions.name: R&R Communication and Employee Engagement
dimensions.definition: Ability to implement, explain, and promote R&R policies, programs, and criteria to officials and employees.

levels.Emerging: Assists in disseminating R&R policies and program information.
levels.Developing: Independently communicates routine R&R requirements and supports implementation.
levels.Proficient: Develops communication approaches/materials that improve understanding and engagement.
levels.Advanced: Shapes organization-wide communication strategies for consistent and effective R&R implementation.

dimensions.name: R&R Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Improvement
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor R&R implementation, analyze results, benchmark practices, and recommend improvements.

levels.Emerging: Tracks routine program activities and maintains supporting records.
levels.Developing: Monitors implementation and identifies routine issues or gaps.
levels.Proficient: Evaluates effectiveness, benchmarks practices, and recommends evidence-based improvements.
levels.Advanced: Leads evaluation of the R&R function and drives system improvements aligned with strategic goals.

competencies.name: Human Resource Records and Information Management
competencies.definition: The ability to receive, validate, organize, maintain, protect, retrieve, and use human resource records and personnel information throughout the records life cycle in accordance with applicable policies, standards, confidentiality requirements, and authorized information systems.

dimensions.name: HR Records Lifecycle Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to receive, classify, organize, retain, retrieve, and release HR records throughout their lifecycle.

levels.Emerging: Receives and releases HR records using an established method/checklist with guidance.
levels.Developing: Validates, organizes, and manages records in accordance with prescribed procedures and disposition schedules.
levels.Proficient: Introduces strategies that improve records management and uses records information as inputs to HR services.
levels.Advanced: Oversees the full HR-records lifecycle and establishes improvements that strengthen accessibility, integrity, and accountability.

dimensions.name: Records Accuracy, Validation, and Disposition Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to validate HR records and ensure completeness, accuracy, retention, and disposition in accordance with prescribed requirements.

levels.Emerging: Checks routine records for completeness and obvious discrepancies with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently validates records and corrects or refers deficiencies.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex records discrepancies and strengthens compliance controls.
levels.Advanced: Establishes records-quality standards and provides expert direction on complex records-compliance issues.

dimensions.name: Confidentiality and Information Security
dimensions.definition: Ability to protect personal, sensitive, and confidential HR information from unauthorized access, loss, or disclosure.

levels.Emerging: Follows established confidentiality and safekeeping procedures.
levels.Developing: Independently applies appropriate access, storage, and release controls.
levels.Proficient: Identifies and manages complex confidentiality or information-security risks.
levels.Advanced: Establishes or improves controls for protection of sensitive HR information and accountable access.

dimensions.name: HRIS and Personnel Information Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain and use authorized personnel information systems, including the Human Resource Information System (HRIS), and HR data to support HR services and transactions.

levels.Emerging: Uses prescribed manual/electronic HR records systems with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently maintains and retrieves HR information using authorized systems and responds to routine HRIS requests.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes HRIS/data issues and improves data accuracy and workflow within authority.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on HRIS/data governance and contributes to system integration and improvement.

dimensions.name: HR Information, Reporting, and Decision Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to provide complete, accurate, and timely personnel information for reporting, service delivery, planning, and authorized management decision-making.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine records and supporting information for reports with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently provides accurate records and routine personnel information for submissions/services.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex information requests and uses validated data to support HR analysis.
levels.Advanced: Uses HR information strategically to support management decisions, service improvement, and organizational planning.

competencies.name: Organizational Profiling and HR Systems Planning
competencies.definition: The ability to understand and analyze the Department’s organizational structure, functions, workforce profile, and HR systems and use relevant information to support workforce planning, organizational development, policy implementation, and HR decision-making within the assigned scope.

dimensions.name: Organizational Structure and Functional Analysis
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand and analyze organizational/functional charts, position descriptions, roles, reporting relationships, and job requirements.

levels.Emerging: Explains basic organizational/functional charts and position information with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently explains roles, reporting relationships, and job requirements for routine HR work.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex organizational/functional relationships and identifies HR implications.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert organizational analysis that informs structural, staffing, or HR-system decisions.

dimensions.name: Workforce and Organizational Profiling
dimensions.definition: Ability to compile, validate, and analyze workforce characteristics, staffing information, personnel movements, and organizational profiles.

levels.Emerging: Compiles routine workforce and staffing information with guidance.
levels.Developing: Maintains accurate workforce profiles and personnel-movement information.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes workforce profiles to identify trends, gaps, and HR implications.
levels.Advanced: Leads workforce/organizational profiling approaches that support strategic planning and management decisions.

dimensions.name: HR Policy and Organizational Environment
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand and explain applicable oversight-agency and internally prescribed HR policies, rules, and regulations affecting Department operations and personnel.

levels.Emerging: Identifies applicable HR policies and rules using prescribed references.
levels.Developing: Explains relevant policies and applies them to routine HR situations.
levels.Proficient: Interprets complex policy requirements and advises on organizational implications.
levels.Advanced: Provides authoritative guidance on the HR policy environment and supports policy/system alignment.

dimensions.name: Workforce Planning and HR Systems Integration
dimensions.definition: Ability to use workforce information to support staffing, HR system linkages, and organizational priorities within assigned authority.

levels.Emerging: Uses approved staffing information and HR-system inputs for assigned tasks.
levels.Developing: Independently links routine workforce information to HR transactions and planning.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes linkages among staffing, HR records, and other HR systems to improve planning.
levels.Advanced: Leads integration of workforce information and HR systems to support strategic workforce priorities.

dimensions.name: Organizational Development and Change Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to contribute to organizational development, restructuring, and change-management activities within assigned HR functions.

levels.Emerging: Participates in assigned organizational-development or change activities with guidance.
levels.Developing: Supports routine change activities and communicates relevant HR implications.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes change impacts and recommends practical HR interventions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert HR input to organizational development, restructuring, and change initiatives.

competencies.name: HR Policy, Process, and Service Delivery Management
competencies.definition: The ability to establish, enhance, execute, and continuously improve HR policies, procedures, systems, and services to ensure compliant, accurate, timely, consistent, and responsive delivery to internal and external clients.

dimensions.name: HR Policy and Process Enhancement
dimensions.definition: Ability to draft, review, enhance, and implement HR policies, procedures, systems, and formal issuances within assigned authority.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing routine HR policies, procedures, or issuances using prescribed formats.
levels.Developing: Independently prepares routine advisories, memoranda, or process improvements.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex policy/process documents and resolves substantive deficiencies.
levels.Advanced: Leads development/review of high-impact HR policies and system/process improvements.

dimensions.name: HR Service Delivery and Client Responsiveness
dimensions.definition: Ability to deliver accurate, accessible, timely, and responsive HR services to employees, applicants, management, and other authorized clients.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine HR services using established procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently manages routine HR requests and communicates requirements clearly.
levels.Proficient: Resolves complex service issues and improves client-response approaches within authority.
levels.Advanced: Leads service-delivery improvements that strengthen accessibility, consistency, and employee/client experience.

dimensions.name: Quality, Timeliness, and Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to ensure HR deliverables meet prescribed quality, documentary, and service-standard requirements, including applicable Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) timelines.

levels.Emerging: Tracks assigned deliverables and meets prescribed timelines with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently manages routine transactions and consistently meets service standards.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex workloads, resolves causes of delay, and maintains quality/compliance.
levels.Advanced: Establishes stronger service controls and systems that sustain timely, reliable, and compliant HR delivery.

dimensions.name: HR Coordination and Compliance Assurance
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate with internal units, management, CSC, DBM, and other relevant offices/agencies and follow through on compliance requirements.

levels.Emerging: Provides information and follows coordination procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently coordinates routine submissions, meetings, and follow-up actions.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex coordination and resolves deficiencies or compliance issues.
levels.Advanced: Provides strategic direction on cross-office/agency coordination and strengthens compliance mechanisms.

dimensions.name: Reporting, Advisory Support, and Management Information
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare internal/external reportorial requirements and provide validated HR information and technical inputs for management planning and decision-making.

levels.Emerging: Provides information for routine reports and management requests with guidance.
levels.Developing: Independently prepares routine reports and accurate technical inputs.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex HR information and provides evidence-based advice for management action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert HR advisory support and improves management-information/reporting systems.

careerProgression.meaning: Demonstrates basic awareness and understanding of the competency. Performs tasks with close guidance and applies standard procedures in familiar situations.

Demonstrates working knowledge and applies the competency with some independence. Handles routine tasks and moderately complex situations using established procedures and seeks guidance when necessary.
Demonstrates strong and consistent application of the competency. Independently handles complex situations, exercises sound judgment, and may guide or support others in applying the competency.

Demonstrates mastery of the competency and applies it strategically across complex and changing situations. Provides direction, mentors others, drives improvements, and contributes to organizational policies, systems, or strategic outcomes.

competencies.name: Patient Care
competencies.definition: Provides comprehensive, safe, responsive, and patient-centered dental care, from oral assessment and initial diagnosis through appropriate treatment, follow-up, health education, and continuity of care, while protecting patient welfare and rights.

dimensions.name: Patient Assessment and Diagnosis
dimensions.definition: Ability to conduct oral/dental assessment, recognize patient needs and conditions, and establish appropriate initial or clinical findings.

levels.Emerging: Performs basic dental/oral check-up and records relevant findings with close guidance.
levels.Developing: Conducts routine assessment, documents oral conditions, and identifies appropriate next steps using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Independently integrates patient history, examination findings, and diagnostic information in complex cases and exercises sound clinical judgment.
levels.Advanced: Provides direction on comprehensive patient assessment approaches and promotes consistent, evidence-informed clinical practice.

dimensions.name: Treatment Planning and Care
dimensions.definition: Ability to determine and provide appropriate dental care based on patient condition, needs, treatment options, and applicable standards.

levels.Emerging: Supports routine patient care and follows established treatment procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Provides appropriate routine dental care and develops or supports treatment plans within role authority.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex cases, evaluates treatment options, and adjusts care based on patient needs and clinical findings.
levels.Advanced: Leads improvements in patient-care approaches and promotes consistent, high-quality, patient-centered dental services.

dimensions.name: Patient Safety and Continuity
dimensions.definition: Ability to protect patient safety, maintain appropriate care conditions, and ensure continuity of dental care and follow-up.

levels.Emerging: Applies basic safety and care procedures and reports concerns promptly.
levels.Developing: Maintains safe care conditions and follows up routine patient-care requirements.
levels.Proficient: Anticipates patient-safety and continuity risks and coordinates appropriate preventive or corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Establishes patient-safety and continuity mechanisms and drives sustained improvements in dental care delivery.

dimensions.name: Patient Communication and Education
dimensions.definition: Ability to communicate dental findings, instructions, preventive information, and treatment options clearly and compassionately.

levels.Emerging: Provides basic instructions using established guidance.
levels.Developing: Explains routine dental care, preventive practices, and follow-up requirements clearly.
levels.Proficient: Communicates complex treatment information, supports informed patient decisions, and responds appropriately to concerns.
levels.Advanced: Promotes patient-centered communication standards and develops approaches that strengthen dental health literacy and trust.

competencies.name: Dental Knowledge
competencies.definition: Applies current and relevant knowledge of dental conditions, diagnosis, prevention, treatment, techniques, and emerging practices to support safe, effective, and continuously improving dental services.

dimensions.name: Dental Knowledge and Clinical Application
dimensions.definition: Ability to apply knowledge of dental conditions, prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and related oral health concepts.

levels.Emerging: Demonstrates basic knowledge of common dental conditions and standard procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies working dental knowledge to routine cases and seeks guidance for unfamiliar conditions.
levels.Proficient: Integrates advanced dental knowledge to address complex cases and supports sound clinical decisions.
levels.Advanced: Serves as a technical resource on complex dental matters and promotes current evidence-informed practice.

dimensions.name: Research and Evidence-Informed Practice
dimensions.definition: Ability to locate, assess, organize, and use relevant information to improve dental methods and services.

levels.Emerging: Uses reliable online sources to learn new dental methods and techniques with guidance.
levels.Developing: Gathers and organizes relevant information and identifies useful evidence for routine practice.
levels.Proficient: Evaluates and validates methods or techniques and applies relevant findings to improve services.
levels.Advanced: Leads practice-informed research or improvement initiatives and translates evidence into enhanced dental practice or policy.

dimensions.name: Continuing Professional Development
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify, evaluate, and pursue relevant learning opportunities to maintain and enhance dental competence.

levels.Emerging: Identifies relevant seminars, webinars, or learning opportunities with guidance.
levels.Developing: Selects relevant training opportunities and applies learning to routine practice.
levels.Proficient: Evaluates the relevance of learning opportunities and integrates acquired knowledge into practice.
levels.Advanced: Shapes continuing professional development priorities and shares learning through mentoring, coaching, or organizational learning activities.

dimensions.name: Dental Service Knowledge Sharing
dimensions.definition: Ability to organize and share dental knowledge and good practices with colleagues and stakeholders.

levels.Emerging: Shares basic information with colleagues when requested.
levels.Developing: Communicates useful dental information and practical learning to others.
levels.Proficient: Provides technical guidance and supports colleagues in applying new knowledge or techniques.
levels.Advanced: Mentors dental personnel, promotes knowledge-sharing practices, and contributes to organizational capability development.

competencies.name: Professional, Legal, and Ethical Dental Practice
competencies.definition: Practices dentistry in accordance with professional standards, applicable laws, ethical principles, confidentiality requirements, patient rights, informed decision-making, and the best interests of patients.

dimensions.name: Professional and Ethical Standards
dimensions.definition: Ability to apply professional ethics, standards of practice, and appropriate conduct in dental service delivery.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic professional and ethical requirements and follows established guidance.
levels.Developing: Consistently applies professional and ethical standards in routine dental practice.
levels.Proficient: Exercises sound ethical judgment in complex or sensitive patient situations.
levels.Advanced: Provides professional leadership and promotes a culture of ethical, patient-centered dental practice.

dimensions.name: Legal and Regulatory Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand and comply with laws, regulations, policies, and standards governing dental practice.

levels.Emerging: Identifies basic legal and regulatory requirements with guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies relevant requirements to routine dental practice and documentation.
levels.Proficient: Interprets requirements in complex cases and recommends appropriate compliant actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert guidance on dental practice compliance and contributes to improved systems, protocols, or policies.

dimensions.name: Confidentiality and Data Privacy
dimensions.definition: Ability to safeguard patient information and maintain confidentiality in accordance with applicable rules and data privacy requirements.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes confidentiality requirements and follows established safeguards.
levels.Developing: Protects patient information in routine records, communication, and service delivery.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex confidentiality and information-sharing situations using sound judgment.

dimensions.name: Troubleshooting and Technical Maintenance
dimensions.definition: Ability to diagnose, resolve, and prevent basic to complex technical issues affecting systems and devices.

levels.Emerging: Conducts routine virus and malware checks and follows preventive system maintenance practices.
levels.Developing: Identifies problems and performs troubleshooting activities for hardware and software issues.
levels.Proficient: Diagnoses complex technical issues and implements corrective actions to minimize service interruptions.
levels.Advanced: Trains and mentors others on troubleshooting methods, maintenance procedures, and technology management practices.

dimensions.name: Data Backup and Information Preservation

levels.Emerging: Maintains files and electronic records in an organized manner.
levels.Developing: Demonstrates awareness of data protection, storage, and backup requirements.
levels.Proficient: Performs systematic backup procedures and prepares databases of information for operational use and continuity.
levels.Advanced: Leads data preservation initiatives and recovers erased or corrupted data to ensure business continuity and information availability.

dimensions.name: Technology Improvement and Advisory
dimensions.definition: Ability to evaluate, recommend, and promote technologies, tools, and process improvements that enhance organizational effectiveness.

levels.Emerging: Uses technologies to access information and enhance individual productivity.
levels.Developing: Utilizes technology to support research, collaboration, and communication through professional networks.
levels.Proficient: Recommends updated technologies, ICT solutions, and process improvements that enhance operations.
levels.Advanced: Evaluates vendors and suppliers, recommends policy enhancements, and promotes technology-driven innovation across the organization.

competencies.name: Presentation Skills
competencies.definition: The ability to express oneself in a clear, concise, organized, and persuasive manner during individual or group situations to communicate information, influence understanding, and support organizational objectives.

dimensions.name: Presentation Delivery

levels.Emerging: Delivers information in a clear, concise, and logical manner to individuals or small groups.
levels.Developing: Uses appropriate vocabulary and communication styles suited to the audience and confidently presents ideas and opinions in larger groups.
levels.Proficient: Delivers assigned topics effectively and adjusts presentation approaches to achieve communication objectives.
levels.Advanced: Plans and delivers high-impact messages that influence decisions, promote understanding, and support organizational initiatives.

dimensions.name: Audience Engagement
dimensions.definition: Ability to sustain audience interest and facilitate participation through appropriate presentation techniques and delivery methods.

levels.Emerging: Uses a variety of presentation methods to maintain audience focus and participation.
levels.Developing: Keeps audiences engaged through effective presentation techniques, illustrations, examples, and interactive approaches.
levels.Proficient: Commands attention and effectively manages group dynamics during presentations and discussions.
levels.Advanced: Designs and facilitates presentations that encourage participation, collaboration, and stakeholder commitment.

dimensions.name: Technical Presentation and Facilitation
dimensions.definition: Ability to present technical information using appropriate visual aids, tools, and communication approaches.

levels.Emerging: Uses visual aids and available resources to support presentations.
levels.Developing: Makes formal presentations using audio-visual equipment and appropriate presentation technologies.
levels.Proficient: Presents technical concepts, project updates, and ICT-related information in a manner understandable to diverse audiences.
levels.Advanced: Communicates complex technical information to decision-makers and stakeholders while promoting informed action and support.

dimensions.name: Knowledge Sharing and Coaching
dimensions.definition: Ability to transfer knowledge, provide guidance, and improve understanding through coaching, mentoring, and presentation activities.

levels.Emerging: Shares information and work-related knowledge with colleagues when needed.
levels.Developing: Participates in discussions and contributes insights that support team learning and understanding.
levels.Proficient: Guides and coaches others on work outputs and provides constructive suggestions to improve quality and clarity.
levels.Advanced: Reviews technical reports and presentation materials, mentors personnel, and promotes continuous learning and knowledge transfer across the organization.

competencies.name: Communications Proficiency
competencies.definition: The ability to convey clear and convincing ideas, opinions, and information through written, verbal, and virtual platforms relative to coordination, negotiation, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.

dimensions.name: Verbal Communication
dimensions.definition: Ability to express ideas, information, and responses clearly, accurately, and professionally through oral communication.

levels.Emerging: Orally presents ideas and facts in a clear, organized, and appropriate manner. Communicates ideas clearly and provides courteous, accurate, and complete responses.
levels.Developing: Speaks in a concise and organized manner appropriate to the audience and situation. Demonstrates active listening and understanding of others' perspectives.
levels.Proficient: Facilitates discussions, clarifies issues, and communicates recommendations effectively to stakeholders and decision-makers.
levels.Advanced: Leads complex discussions, promotes consensus, and influences decisions through effective communication strategies.

dimensions.name: Written Communication
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, organize, edit, and communicate written information effectively using appropriate formats and language.

levels.Emerging: Uses business communication formats and prepares routine correspondence based on available information.
levels.Developing: Secures information from references and prepares routine communications, reports, memoranda, and technical documents. Self-edits written work for accuracy and completeness.
levels.Proficient: Produces clear, concise, and well-structured reports, proposals, and documentation with minimal revisions required.
levels.Advanced: Develops standards for written communication, ensures organizational consistency, and produces high-impact professional documents supporting strategic objectives.

dimensions.name: Stakeholder Communication and Collaboration
dimensions.definition: Ability to establish productive communication channels and relationships that facilitate coordination, collaboration, and achievement of organizational objectives.

levels.Emerging: Shares information with colleagues and participates in routine coordination activities.
levels.Developing: Creates opportunities for stakeholders to express opinions, ideas, and concerns through active and empathetic engagement.
levels.Proficient: Facilitates open exchange of ideas, resolves communication barriers, and strengthens collaboration among stakeholders.
levels.Advanced: Builds strategic relationships, negotiates agreements, and establishes communication mechanisms that improve organizational effectiveness.

dimensions.name: Technical and Professional Communication
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, and communicate technical information, reports, recommendations, and project-related documentation.

levels.Emerging: Documents work-related information accurately and communicates technical concepts using understandable language.
levels.Developing: Prepares technical reports, project-related documents, and analytical summaries involving interrelated information.
levels.Proficient: Drafts, edits, revises, and reviews technical reports, proposals, and correspondence for management consideration.
levels.Advanced: Reviews and validates complex technical communications, ensuring clarity, completeness, accuracy, and alignment with organizational requirements.

competencies.name: Procurement Process and Administration
competencies.definition: The ability to understand, assess, and validate procurement processes involving the acquisition of goods and services while ensuring compliance with governing rules, regulations, and standards supporting project implementation and organizational objectives.

dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, validate, and maintain procurement documents while ensuring adherence to procurement laws, policies, and procedural requirements.

levels.Developing: Uses checklists to review completeness and consistency of procurement documents and supporting requirements.

levels.Advanced: Establishes controls and review mechanisms that strengthen compliance, transparency, and accountability in procurement activities.

levels.Proficient: Verifies records, approvals, and procurement requirements and evaluates procurement activities for compliance and completeness.
levels.Advanced: Assesses procurement risks, identifies process gaps, and recommends improvements that support effective procurement management.

dimensions.definition: Ability to provide guidance, address concerns, and coordinate procurement activities with stakeholders while ensuring compliance and efficiency.

levels.Advanced: Engages key stakeholders in procurement planning and execution and promotes best practices that support organizational goals.

levels.Proficient: Monitors procurement activities, prepares procurement reports, and identifies compliance issues requiring management action.
levels.Advanced: Recommends process improvements, streamlines procurement procedures, and promotes continuous enhancement of procurement governance and compliance systems.

dimensions.definition: Ability to evaluate ICT specifications, validate technical requirements, conduct acceptance testing, and provide technical recommendations supporting ICT procurement activities.

levels.Proficient: Conducts technical assessments, acceptance testing, and technical validation of ICT procurements and project deliverables.
levels.Advanced: Develops technical evaluation standards, recommends ICT solutions, advises management on technology acquisitions, and leads complex ICT procurement evaluations.

competencies.name: Troubleshooting and Problem-Solving
competencies.definition: The ability to systematically identify, analyze, diagnose, and resolve hardware, software, network, application, and operational issues in a timely and effective manner to ensure continuity of ICT services and minimize disruptions to organizational operations.

levels.Developing: Gathers relevant information, analyzes symptoms, and determines probable causes of technical problems.
levels.Proficient: Performs root-cause analysis and evaluates multiple factors affecting system or operational performance.
levels.Advanced: Leads complex diagnostic activities involving interconnected systems, applications, infrastructure, and processes.

dimensions.name: Technical Resolution and Corrective Action
dimensions.definition: Ability to implement appropriate solutions and corrective measures to address identified problems and restore normal operations.

levels.Developing: Applies troubleshooting techniques to resolve hardware, software, network, and application issues independently.
levels.Proficient: Implements corrective solutions that address complex technical issues while minimizing operational disruption.
levels.Advanced: Designs and recommends strategic solutions that improve system reliability, performance, and service delivery.

dimensions.name: Incident Management and Service Recovery
dimensions.definition: Ability to manage incidents, minimize disruptions, restore services, and ensure business continuity.

levels.Proficient: Manages incident resolution activities and ensures service recovery within prescribed timelines.
levels.Advanced: Leads incident response, service restoration efforts, and business continuity activities during major disruptions.

levels.Proficient: Evaluates trends and develops recommendations to improve system performance and reduce future incidents.
levels.Advanced: Establishes continuous improvement practices, preventive maintenance programs, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms to strengthen organizational resilience.

competencies.name: IT Asset Lifecycle Management

levels.Advanced: Develops strategic plans and recommendations for ICT asset acquisition aligned with organizational priorities and technology roadmaps.

dimensions.definition: Ability to install, configure, deploy, track, and optimize ICT assets to support operational requirements.

levels.Emerging: Assists in installation, configuration, and deployment of ICT assets.

levels.Proficient: Manages deployment activities and monitors asset utilization to maximize operational effectiveness.
levels.Advanced: Establishes deployment strategies and asset optimization initiatives that improve service delivery and resource efficiency.

dimensions.name: Asset Maintenance and Monitoring
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor asset condition, conduct maintenance activities, manage inventories, and ensure operational readiness.

levels.Proficient: Ensures compliance with policies governing asset accountability, disposal, replacement, and renewal.
levels.Advanced: Establishes governance mechanisms, lifecycle policies, and asset management strategies that optimize cost, compliance, and asset value throughout the organization.

levels.Advanced: Develops cloud resiliency, disaster recovery, scalability, and service optimization frameworks supporting organizational operations.

competencies.name: IT Project Management

levels.Emerging: Supports assigned project monitoring and documentation activities using established procedures, checklists and communication channels.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine to moderately complex project monitoring and documentation activities with increasing independence; tracks actions and follows through on commitments.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex project monitoring and documentation, resolves issues, coordinates stakeholders and provides timely, well-supported advice.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership for project monitoring and documentation, mentors others, improves coordination systems and contributes to strategic governance and organizational outcomes.

dimensions.name: Risk, Issue and Change Management
dimensions.definition: Identifies and assesses project risks, manages issues and changes, and escalates matters requiring management intervention.

levels.Emerging: Supports assigned risk, issue and change management activities using established procedures, checklists and communication channels.

levels.Emerging: Supports assigned technical advisory and communication activities using established procedures, checklists and communication channels.
levels.Developing: Coordinates routine to moderately complex technical advisory and communication activities with increasing independence; tracks actions and follows through on commitments.

name: Contract Management Division
sourceFile: Contract Management Division_Revised Competency Framework Initial Draft.docx

careerProgression.meaning: Performs routine work with close guidance and follows established procedures.
Applies the competency with increasing independence to routine and moderately complex work and seeks guidance when necessary.
Independently handles complex work, exercises sound judgment, resolves issues, and may guide or support others.
Provides expert direction, mentors others, drives improvements, and contributes to systems, standards, policies, or strategic outcomes.

competencies.name: Government Procurement Systems and Regulatory Compliance
competencies.definition: The ability to implement and administer government procurement requirements and related regulatory processes in accordance with applicable procurement laws, rules, regulations, Commission on Audit (COA) requirements, and Department procedures, including contract-document posting, transparency, blacklisting, and regulatory submissions.

dimensions.name: Procurement Law and Regulatory Application
dimensions.definition: Ability to understand and apply current procurement laws, rules, regulations, and government requirements.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes applicable requirements and follows established procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies applicable requirements to routine transactions and identifies when clarification is needed.
levels.Proficient: Interprets requirements in complex transactions and provides sound technical guidance.
levels.Advanced: Provides authoritative guidance on complex compliance issues and contributes to improved controls or policy implementation.

dimensions.name: Procurement Documentation and Posting
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, submit, and post required procurement and contract documents through prescribed channels.

levels.Emerging: Assists in assembling and checking routine documents for completeness.
levels.Developing: Prepares and processes routine documents for posting using prescribed procedures.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex posting requirements and resolves documentation deficiencies.
levels.Advanced: Establishes document-quality and posting controls that strengthen timeliness, accuracy, transparency, and compliance.

dimensions.name: Transparency and Regulatory Reporting
dimensions.definition: Ability to comply with transparency and reporting requirements through the DOTr website, Modernized PhilGEPS, Commission on Audit (COA), DepDev, and other prescribed channels.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine submission requirements and follows prescribed processes.
levels.Developing: Completes routine website, PhilGEPS, and regulatory submissions accurately and on time.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex regulatory submissions and resolves deficiencies.
levels.Advanced: Provides direction on transparency/reporting systems and improves controls for sustained compliance.

dimensions.name: Blacklisting and Procurement Enforcement
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, post, monitor, and maintain records of Blacklisting Orders and related enforcement actions within assigned authority.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic blacklisting requirements and routes documents appropriately.
levels.Developing: Processes routine Blacklisting Orders using established requirements.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex blacklisting documentation and coordinates required actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction on blacklisting compliance and strengthens enforcement controls.

dimensions.name: Green Procurement Compliance
dimensions.definition: Ability to apply green and sustainable procurement principles, environmental criteria, and Green Public Procurement (GPP) guidelines when reviewing, administering, and enforcing procurement and contract requirements.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic green and sustainable procurement requirements and follows established procedures with guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies applicable green procurement criteria to routine transactions and identifies when clarification is needed.
levels.Proficient: Interprets green procurement requirements in complex transactions and provides sound technical guidance on sustainable sourcing options.
levels.Advanced: Provides authoritative guidance on green procurement compliance and contributes to improved controls or policy implementation for sustainable procurement.

competencies.name: Contract Management and Administration
competencies.definition: The ability to efficiently manage and administer contracts through preparation, review, execution, monitoring, modification, compliance, documentation, payment support, and closure, while managing risks and coordinating with end-user units and stakeholders.

dimensions.name: Contract Preparation and Review
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, validate, and endorse contract documents and related certifications.

levels.Emerging: Assists in preparing routine contract documents using prescribed formats.
levels.Developing: Prepares and reviews routine contract documents and identifies deficiencies.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex contracts, resolves issues, and recommends appropriate action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on complex contract documentation and establishes quality standards.

dimensions.name: Post-Award Contract Administration
dimensions.definition: Ability to monitor and administer contract obligations, milestones, amendments, extensions, suspension, termination, and other post-award requirements.

levels.Emerging: Maintains basic contract information and supports routine post-award actions.
levels.Developing: Monitors routine contract requirements and processes routine post-award actions.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex post-award issues and advises on contract risks and compliance.
levels.Advanced: Provides strategic direction on post-award administration and improves contract governance.

dimensions.name: Contract Compliance and Risk Management
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify deviations, assess contract risks, and support appropriate corrective, preventive, or enforcement actions.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common deviations and reports concerns with guidance.
levels.Developing: Monitors routine compliance and documents deviations using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes complex deviations and risks and recommends or coordinates corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert advice on significant risks and establishes stronger compliance controls.

dimensions.name: End-User Coordination and Payment Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate with end-user units on acceptance, required contract documents, and timely payment processing.

levels.Emerging: Provides routine contract documents or information with guidance.
levels.Developing: Provides required certified contract documents and supports routine acceptance/payment requirements.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates complex end-user concerns and resolves documentation issues affecting acceptance or payment.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens coordination mechanisms and improves contract acceptance, documentation, and payment support.

competencies.name: Contract and Procurement Data and Records Management
competencies.definition: The ability to collate, validate, organize, protect, retrieve, maintain, and manage contract and procurement data and records to ensure integrity, reliability, accessibility, and timely submission.

dimensions.name: Data Accuracy and Validation
dimensions.definition: Ability to verify completeness, accuracy, consistency, and reliability of contract and procurement information.

levels.Emerging: Checks routine data for obvious errors or missing information with guidance.
levels.Developing: Verifies routine transaction details and corrects or reports discrepancies.
levels.Proficient: Validates complex datasets and resolves or escalates material discrepancies.
levels.Advanced: Establishes data-quality controls and standards that strengthen reliability and decision support.

dimensions.name: Records Organization and Retrieval
dimensions.definition: Ability to organize and maintain records in a logical, coherent, secure, and retrievable manner.

levels.Emerging: Files and stores routine records according to established procedures.
levels.Developing: Maintains organized records and retrieves requested information promptly.
levels.Proficient: Improves classification, retrieval, and control of complex records.
levels.Advanced: Designs or improves systems for efficient, reliable, and secure records retrieval.

dimensions.name: Electronic and Physical Records Safekeeping
dimensions.definition: Ability to protect electronic and hard-copy procurement and contract records throughout their required retention and use.

levels.Emerging: Follows established storage and safekeeping procedures.
levels.Developing: Ensures proper documentation and safekeeping of assigned electronic and hard-copy records.
levels.Proficient: Monitors records integrity and addresses security, completeness, or accessibility risks.
levels.Advanced: Provides direction on records-protection controls and strengthens records-management practices.

dimensions.name: Records Compliance and Reporting
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain and submit required records and supporting documents to Commission on Audit (COA), DepDev, end-users, and other authorized recipients.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine records and supporting documents for submission with guidance.
levels.Developing: Processes routine submissions and maintains evidence of transmittal or receipt.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex records submissions and resolves deficiencies or follow-up requirements.
levels.Advanced: Establishes reliable records-compliance systems and provides technical guidance on complex submissions.

competencies.name: Communications and Stakeholder Coordination
competencies.definition: The ability to convey clear, accurate, timely, and appropriate information through written, verbal, and virtual platforms to support contract review, procurement compliance, coordination, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.

dimensions.name: Clear and Accurate Communication
dimensions.definition: Ability to communicate information clearly, accurately, completely, and appropriately for the audience and purpose.

levels.Emerging: Communicates routine information clearly using established formats and channels.
levels.Developing: Provides clear and accurate routine communications and responds appropriately.
levels.Proficient: Communicates complex requirements and issues clearly, adapting the message to the audience.
levels.Advanced: Shapes communication approaches for sensitive or high-impact matters and promotes communication standards.

dimensions.name: Written Contract and Procurement Communication
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare, review, and improve memoranda, letters, certifications, reports, requests, and other CMD documents.

levels.Emerging: Prepares routine correspondence using available information and prescribed formats.
levels.Developing: Prepares clear routine memoranda, letters, certifications, and reports with minimal guidance.
levels.Proficient: Drafts and reviews complex communications and ensures technical accuracy.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert review and guidance on high-level or sensitive written communications.

dimensions.name: Stakeholder Coordination
dimensions.definition: Ability to coordinate effectively with end-users, PMOs, ProcMS offices, Commission on Audit (COA), DepDev, and other stakeholders.

levels.Emerging: Coordinates routine matters with guidance and follows up on assigned actions.
levels.Developing: Independently coordinates routine requirements and clarifies information.
levels.Proficient: Manages complex cross-functional coordination and resolves communication gaps.
levels.Advanced: Builds effective coordination mechanisms and provides direction on complex stakeholder matters.

dimensions.name: Communication for Compliance and Decision Support
dimensions.definition: Ability to explain requirements, surface issues, and communicate information that supports compliant decisions and appropriate action.

levels.Emerging: Provides basic explanations of established requirements and escalates concerns.
levels.Developing: Explains routine procurement and contract requirements accurately.
levels.Proficient: Presents complex compliance or contract issues and recommends appropriate actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides authoritative communication support for high-level decisions, policy implementation, and organizational risk management.

name: Procurement Planning and Management Division
sourceFile: Planning and Procurement Management Division_Revised Competency Framework Initial Draft.docx

careerProgression.meaning: Demonstrates basic awareness and understanding; performs routine tasks using established procedures with close guidance.
Applies working knowledge independently to routine and moderately complex work; follows established procedures and seeks guidance for exceptions.
Consistently handles complex work independently, exercises sound judgment, reviews outputs, and provides technical support to others.
Demonstrates mastery across complex and changing situations; provides direction, mentors others, strengthens controls/processes, and contributes to organizational improvements.

competencies.name: Procurement Planning and Technical Document Review
competencies.definition: The ability to systematically evaluate, analyze, and endorse procurement documents for completeness, accuracy, technical sufficiency, compliance, and alignment with applicable procurement requirements and organizational priorities.

dimensions.name: Document Completeness and Technical Sufficiency
dimensions.definition: Ability to examine PPMPs, technical specifications, ABC/estimated budget, quotations, market study/scoping documents, and supporting requirements for completeness and adequacy.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine document completeness and technical sufficiency tasks using prescribed procedures and checklists with close guidance; identifies basic documentary or process requirements.
levels.Developing: Independently performs routine and moderately complex document completeness and technical sufficiency activities, applies established requirements, and appropriately escalates exceptions or unclear cases.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex document completeness and technical sufficiency cases, exercises sound judgment in resolving issues, reviews outputs for quality and compliance, and provides technical assistance to colleagues.
levels.Advanced: Serves as an organizational resource for document completeness and technical sufficiency, provides direction on complex or changing cases, mentors others, strengthens controls or processes, and recommends improvements.

dimensions.name: Procurement Compliance Review
dimensions.definition: Ability to assess submitted procurement documents against applicable procurement rules, prescribed procedures, documentary requirements, and the appropriate procurement modality.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine procurement compliance review tasks using prescribed procedures and checklists with close guidance; identifies basic documentary or process requirements.
levels.Developing: Independently performs routine and moderately complex procurement compliance review activities, applies established requirements, and appropriately escalates exceptions or unclear cases.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex procurement compliance review cases, exercises sound judgment in resolving issues, reviews outputs for quality and compliance, and provides technical assistance to colleagues.
levels.Advanced: Serves as an organizational resource for procurement compliance review, provides direction on complex or changing cases, mentors others, strengthens controls or processes, and recommends improvements.

dimensions.name: Evaluation, Recommendation and Endorsement
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify deficiencies, formulate clear comments or recommendations, and endorse compliant procurement documents within prescribed timelines.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine evaluation, recommendation and endorsement tasks using prescribed procedures and checklists with close guidance; identifies basic documentary or process requirements.
levels.Developing: Independently performs routine and moderately complex evaluation, recommendation and endorsement activities, applies established requirements, and appropriately escalates exceptions or unclear cases.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex evaluation, recommendation and endorsement cases, exercises sound judgment in resolving issues, reviews outputs for quality and compliance, and provides technical assistance to colleagues.
levels.Advanced: Serves as an organizational resource for evaluation, recommendation and endorsement, provides direction on complex or changing cases, mentors others, strengthens controls or processes, and recommends improvements.

competencies.name: Procurement Action Document and Issuance Preparation
competencies.definition: The ability to prepare accurate, complete, and timely procurement action documents, issuances, and related official documents required for the conduct and administration of procurement activities.

dimensions.name: Drafting and Document Development
dimensions.definition: Ability to prepare procurement action documents, issuances, memoranda, and similar documents using prescribed formats, references, and supporting information.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine drafting and document development tasks using prescribed procedures and checklists with close guidance; identifies basic documentary or process requirements.
levels.Developing: Independently performs routine and moderately complex drafting and document development activities, applies established requirements, and appropriately escalates exceptions or unclear cases.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex drafting and document development cases, exercises sound judgment in resolving issues, reviews outputs for quality and compliance, and provides technical assistance to colleagues.
levels.Advanced: Serves as an organizational resource for drafting and document development, provides direction on complex or changing cases, mentors others, strengthens controls or processes, and recommends improvements.

dimensions.name: Accuracy and Quality Control
dimensions.definition: Ability to verify facts, recommendations, references, attachments, and documentary details and minimize substantive revisions before submission.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine accuracy and quality control tasks using prescribed procedures and checklists with close guidance; identifies basic documentary or process requirements.
levels.Developing: Independently performs routine and moderately complex accuracy and quality control activities, applies established requirements, and appropriately escalates exceptions or unclear cases.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex accuracy and quality control cases, exercises sound judgment in resolving issues, reviews outputs for quality and compliance, and provides technical assistance to colleagues.
levels.Advanced: Serves as an organizational resource for accuracy and quality control, provides direction on complex or changing cases, mentors others, strengthens controls or processes, and recommends improvements.

dimensions.name: Timeliness and Revision Management
