competencies.name: Accounts Reconciliation
competencies.definition: Applies systematic, timely, and accurate reconciliation of accounting control accounts and related financial records to identify, resolve, document, and escalate discrepancies in accordance with applicable accounting rules and reporting requirements.

dimensions.name: Reconciliation Planning and Scheduling
dimensions.definition: The ability to organize, schedule, and monitor required reconciliation activities in accordance with prescribed cycles, deadlines, and reporting requirements.

levels.Emerging: Follows prescribed schedules and checklists for assigned reconciliations.
levels.Developing: Performs assigned reconciliations independently and keeps reconciliation schedules current.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates reconciliation cycles across related accounts and ensures exceptions are acted upon promptly.
levels.Advanced: Establishes division-wide reconciliation priorities and ensures timely completion of critical reconciliations.

dimensions.name: Transaction Matching and Reconciling Items
dimensions.definition: The ability to compare related accounting records and supporting documents, identify reconciling items, trace differences to their sources, and determine appropriate action.

levels.Emerging: Matches supporting records and identifies obvious differences.
levels.Developing: Identifies and documents reconciling items and traces them to source records.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes recurring or complex reconciling items and recommends appropriate adjustments.
levels.Advanced: Directs resolution of material or systemic reconciling issues and determines escalation requirements.

dimensions.name: Adjustments and Error Resolution
dimensions.definition: The ability to identify accounting errors, prepare or validate authorized correcting entries, and resolve discrepancies with adequate support and compliance controls.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes errors and refers unresolved items to the supervisor.
levels.Developing: Prepares or supports authorized correcting entries and clears routine discrepancies.
levels.Proficient: Reviews proposed adjustments for accuracy, support, and compliance.
levels.Advanced: Provides oversight on material adjustments and ensures corrective actions protect the integrity of accounting records.

dimensions.name: Control and Compliance
dimensions.definition: The ability to apply and assess reconciliation controls, Government Accounting Manual (GAM), Commission on Audit (COA), and related requirements to maintain reliable accounting records.

levels.Emerging: Applies prescribed reconciliation procedures and control requirements.
levels.Developing: Uses applicable COA/GAM rules and internal procedures when performing reconciliations.
levels.Proficient: Assesses reconciliation controls and identifies gaps that may affect reporting reliability.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens reconciliation controls and advises management on significant control risks.

dimensions.name: Exception Reporting and Escalation
dimensions.definition: The ability to document, analyze, communicate, and escalate unusual or unresolved reconciliation matters, including recommended corrective actions.

levels.Emerging: Reports unusual or unresolved items to the appropriate supervisor.
levels.Developing: Maintains records of exceptions and communicates status within required timelines.
levels.Proficient: Prepares exception reports with analysis and recommended actions for management.
levels.Advanced: Uses reconciliation results to direct corrective action, audit responses, and operational improvements.

dimensions.name: Management and Audit Support
dimensions.definition: The ability to provide accurate reconciliation information, explanations, and supporting documents to management, auditors, and other authorized stakeholders.

levels.Emerging: Provides supporting documents when requested.
levels.Developing: Responds to routine reconciliation queries and audit requests accurately.
levels.Proficient: Explains reconciliation results and implications to management and auditors.
levels.Advanced: Uses reconciliation trends and audit observations to improve accounting processes and reporting integrity.

competencies.name: Revenues and Expenditures
competencies.definition: Applies accounting processes for revenues and expenditures by accurately recording, reviewing, monitoring, and reporting transactions in accordance with applicable government accounting, budget, procurement, tax, and financial rules.

dimensions.name: Revenue and Expenditure Recording
dimensions.definition: The ability to accurately recognize, classify, record, and review revenue and expenditure transactions using applicable accounting and fund classifications.

levels.Emerging: Records assigned revenue and expenditure transactions using prescribed procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies appropriate account and fund classifications to routine transactions.
levels.Proficient: Reviews transaction classifications and correcting entries for complex or unusual items.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction on appropriate recognition, classification, and treatment of material transactions.

dimensions.name: Transaction and Budget Controls
dimensions.definition: The ability to check revenue and expenditure transactions against budget, authority, supporting records, and other control requirements and address exceptions.

levels.Emerging: Checks assigned transactions against available supporting documents and authority.
levels.Developing: Performs routine control checks between transactions, budget information, and supporting records.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes exceptions between obligations, expenditures, payments, and available budget information.
levels.Advanced: Advises management on significant control issues affecting expenditure and revenue accountability.

dimensions.name: Accruals, Prepayments and Adjustments
dimensions.definition: The ability to recognize, record, review, and validate accruals, prepayments, and other authorized period-end

levels.Emerging: Recognizes routine month-end adjustments under guidance.
levels.Developing: Processes or supports authorized accrual, prepayment, and related adjustments.
levels.Proficient: Reviews the completeness and appropriateness of period-end adjustments.
levels.Advanced: Oversees period-end adjustment practices to improve reliability of financial reporting.

dimensions.name: Compliance and Documentation
dimensions.definition: The ability to maintain complete and supportable transaction documentation and apply applicable COA, DBM, DOF, BIR, procurement, and related financial requirements.

levels.Emerging: Follows applicable accounting and financial rules for assigned transactions.
levels.Developing: Maintains adequate documentation and applies relevant COA, DBM, DOF, BIR and related requirements.
levels.Proficient: Identifies compliance risks in revenue and expenditure transactions and recommends corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides authoritative technical guidance on complex compliance issues within the division's mandate.

dimensions.name: Reporting and Monitoring
dimensions.definition: The ability to prepare, review, and analyze revenue and expenditure information and monitoring reports for accurate and timely financial reporting and management use.

levels.Emerging: Provides accurate transaction data and routine control information.
levels.Developing: Prepares or supports periodic revenue and expenditure monitoring reports.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes trends and variances in revenue and expenditure information for management use.
levels.Advanced: Uses monitoring results to recommend improvements in controls, reporting, and resource use.

dimensions.name: Advisory and Issue Resolution
dimensions.definition: The ability to address accounting concerns on revenues and expenditures, provide appropriate technical assistance, and recommend compliant solutions to recurring or complex issues.

levels.Emerging: Raises transaction issues to the appropriate supervisor.
levels.Developing: Assists clients and staff in resolving routine recording and classification concerns.
levels.Proficient: Provides technical advice on complex revenue and expenditure issues and documents resolutions.
levels.Advanced: Advises management on recurring issues and recommends improvements to accounting practices and controls.

competencies.name: Preparation and Interpretation of Financial Statements and Reports
competencies.definition: Prepares, reviews, consolidates, and interprets financial statements and accounting reports accurately and on time, ensuring compliance with applicable government accounting and reporting requirements and providing information useful for management and oversight.

dimensions.name: Financial Statement Preparation
dimensions.definition: The ability to compile, prepare, review, and validate financial statements and supporting schedules for completeness, accuracy, and timely submission.

levels.Emerging: Assists in assembling information and completing assigned reporting tasks.
levels.Developing: Prepares assigned financial statements and supporting schedules accurately and within deadlines.
levels.Proficient: Reviews financial statements for completeness, consistency, and appropriate adjustments.
levels.Advanced: Provides oversight of major financial reporting outputs and ensures their reliability before submission.

dimensions.name: Month-End and Year-End Closing
dimensions.definition: The ability to perform and coordinate period-end closing activities, entries, reconciliations, and issue resolution to support complete and reliable financial statements.

levels.Emerging: Completes assigned closing activities using prescribed procedures.
levels.Developing: Processes routine closing entries and reconciles supporting schedules.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates complex closing activities and resolves reporting issues affecting period-end balances.
levels.Advanced: Directs closing priorities and ensures timely resolution of material issues affecting financial statements.

dimensions.name: Consolidation and Report Integration
dimensions.definition: The ability to combine and validate financial information from relevant accounting records and reporting units and resolve inconsistencies before submission.

levels.Emerging: Provides accurate data for consolidation and reporting.
levels.Developing: Consolidates assigned reports and supporting schedules using established procedures.
levels.Proficient: Reviews consolidated information and resolves inconsistencies across reporting units.
levels.Advanced: Oversees consolidation processes and advises management on significant reporting differences.

dimensions.name: Analysis and Interpretation
dimensions.definition: The ability to examine financial information, identify trends, variances, and significant movements, and explain their implications for management and oversight.

levels.Emerging: Identifies basic trends or unusual movements in financial information.
levels.Developing: Explains routine variances and relationships among financial accounts.
levels.Proficient: Interprets financial results and identifies implications for management decision-making.
levels.Advanced: Provides strategic financial interpretation and recommends actions based on material trends, risks, and reporting results.

dimensions.name: Regulatory and Management Reporting
dimensions.definition: The ability to prepare and review statutory and management reports in prescribed formats and schedules while meeting applicable government reporting requirements.

levels.Emerging: Follows prescribed formats and submission schedules.
levels.Developing: Prepares required statutory and management reports with complete supporting documentation.
levels.Proficient: Ensures reports meet applicable COA, DBM, DOF, BIR and other oversight requirements.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens reporting systems and advises management on improving quality, timeliness, and usefulness of reports.

dimensions.name: Reporting Quality and Stakeholder Support
dimensions.definition: The ability to ensure the quality and usefulness of financial reports and to explain reporting information and resolve reporting concerns with authorized stakeholders and auditors.

levels.Emerging: Responds accurately to routine reporting requests.
levels.Developing: Clarifies reporting requirements and provides complete supporting information.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates with stakeholders and auditors to resolve reporting issues and explain results.
levels.Advanced: Represents the division in complex reporting discussions and drives resolution of material audit or stakeholder concerns.

competencies.name: Accounting for Current Assets and Current Liabilities
competencies.definition: Applies accounting and control procedures for current assets and current liabilities, including inventories, receivables, payables, advances, and related balances, to maintain accurate, current, and supportable financial information.

dimensions.name: Recognition and Classification
dimensions.definition: The ability to correctly identify, recognize, and classify current assets and current liabilities based on the nature of the transaction and applicable accounting rules.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine current asset and liability transactions using prescribed guidance.
levels.Developing: Applies appropriate account classifications and supporting documentation.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex or unusual current asset and liability transactions for proper recognition.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction on significant recognition and classification issues.

dimensions.name: Receivables and Collections

levels.Emerging: Maintains assigned receivable records and supporting documents.
levels.Developing: Monitors receivable balances and follows up routine discrepancies or aging items.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes outstanding receivables and recommends appropriate accounting or collection actions within the division's authority.
levels.Advanced: Advises management on material receivable issues and recurring collection/accounting risks.

dimensions.name: Payables and Due-and-Demandable Accounts
dimensions.definition: The ability to review, process, and validate accounts payable and due-and-demandable claims for completeness, legality, proper accounting treatment, and settlement.

levels.Emerging: Checks supporting documents for assigned payables.
levels.Developing: Processes or validates routine accounts payable and due-and-demandable claims.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex payable transactions for completeness, legality, and proper accounting treatment.
levels.Advanced: Provides oversight on material payables and strengthens controls over recognition and settlement.

dimensions.name: Advances and Other Current Balances
dimensions.definition: The ability to maintain, monitor, reconcile, and resolve advances and other current balances, including liquidation and aging concerns.

levels.Emerging: Maintains records of assigned advances and related balances.
levels.Developing: Monitors liquidation, aging, and supporting documentation for routine balances.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes long-outstanding advances and recommends appropriate reconciliation or settlement actions.
levels.Advanced: Directs resolution of significant outstanding balances and advises on control improvements.

dimensions.name: Reconciliation and Adjustment
dimensions.definition: The ability to reconcile current asset and liability balances, investigate differences, and validate authorized adjustments before reporting.

levels.Emerging: Performs routine checks between subsidiary records and supporting documents.
levels.Developing: Reconciles assigned current asset and liability balances and clears routine differences.
levels.Proficient: Reviews adjustments and investigates material or recurring discrepancies.
levels.Advanced: Ensures systematic reconciliation and correction of significant balances before reporting.

dimensions.name: Compliance and Reporting
dimensions.definition: The ability to apply asset-accounting requirements and prepare reliable schedules and information for financial reporting, audit, and management purposes.

levels.Emerging: Follows applicable government accounting and financial rules.
levels.Developing: Prepares supporting schedules and information for required reports.
levels.Proficient: Assesses compliance issues and recommends corrective actions affecting current balances.
levels.Advanced: Provides management-level guidance on significant current asset and liability reporting and control matters.

competencies.name: Accounting for Non-Current Assets
competencies.definition: Applies accounting processes and controls for non-current assets, including recognition, recording, depreciation, impairment, revaluation, transfers, and disposal, to support accurate asset records and reliable financial reporting.

dimensions.name: Asset Recognition and Classification
dimensions.definition: The ability to identify, recognize, and classify non-current assets and related expenditures according to applicable accounting rules and authorized classifications.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine non-current asset transactions using prescribed guidance.
levels.Developing: Distinguishes capital asset transactions from recurrent expenditures and applies prescribed classifications.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex acquisition and classification issues and recommends appropriate accounting treatment.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction on significant asset recognition and classification matters.

dimensions.name: Asset Register and Records
dimensions.definition: The ability to maintain complete, accurate, and current asset records and supporting documentation and ensure consistency with source records.

levels.Emerging: Updates or supports maintenance of assigned asset records.
levels.Developing: Maintains accurate asset-register information and supporting documentation.
levels.Proficient: Reviews asset records for completeness, accuracy, and consistency with supporting records.
levels.Advanced: Oversees improvements in asset-record quality and coordinates resolution of significant data gaps.

dimensions.name: Depreciation and Measurement
dimensions.definition: The ability to calculate, record, review, and validate depreciation and other authorized measurement adjustments affecting non-current assets.

levels.Emerging: Applies prescribed depreciation schedules under guidance.
levels.Developing: Calculates or records routine depreciation and related entries accurately.
levels.Proficient: Reviews depreciation, measurement, and authorized adjustments for consistency with applicable rules.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical oversight on significant measurement, impairment, or revaluation matters.

dimensions.name: Transfers, Disposals and Adjustments
dimensions.definition: The ability to process and review authorized asset transfers, disposals, and accounting adjustments with complete documentation and approvals.

levels.Emerging: Processes assigned asset transfers or disposal documentation under guidance.
levels.Developing: Records authorized transfers, disposals, and related accounting entries.
levels.Proficient: Reviews disposal and adjustment transactions and ensures adequate support and approvals.
levels.Advanced: Advises management on significant asset disposal, replacement, impairment, or revaluation issues.

dimensions.name: Asset Reconciliation and Verification

levels.Emerging: Compares assigned asset records with available supporting information.
levels.Developing: Reconciles asset records and investigates routine differences.
levels.Proficient: Coordinates verification and resolution of material discrepancies with asset-holding offices.
levels.Advanced: Uses asset reconciliation results to strengthen controls and reporting across the division.

dimensions.name: Compliance and Reporting
dimensions.definition: The ability to apply asset-accounting requirements and prepare reliable schedules and information for financial reporting, audit, and management purposes.

levels.Emerging: Follows applicable accounting and asset-management procedures.
levels.Developing: Prepares supporting schedules and information for financial reporting.
levels.Proficient: Assesses compliance of asset accounting and identifies areas needing corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Strengthens asset-accounting practices and advises management on reporting integrity and compliance.

competencies.name: Accounting for Debt and Other Liabilities
competencies.definition: Applies appropriate accounting treatment and controls for debt and other liabilities, including loans, leases, provisions, and contingent liabilities, consistent with applicable accounting rules and the division's assigned responsibilities.

dimensions.name: Liability Recognition and Classification
dimensions.definition: The ability to identify, recognize, and classify liabilities accurately based on their nature, terms, and applicable accounting requirements.

levels.Emerging: Identifies routine liability transactions and applies prescribed guidance.
levels.Developing: Classifies liabilities using applicable account and fund codes.
levels.Proficient: Reviews complex liabilities for appropriate recognition and classification.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical direction on material or complex liability accounting issues.

levels.Emerging: Records assigned loan-related transactions using prescribed procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies correct accounting treatment to loan receipts, payments, and related transactions.
levels.Proficient: Reviews loan accounting, source-of-funds coding, and related reconciliations for accuracy.
levels.Advanced: Advises on complex financing-related accounting issues within the division's mandate.

dimensions.name: Lease and Other Liability Accounting
dimensions.definition: The ability to account for leases and other liability transactions, including provisions and contingent liabilities, using applicable recognition and measurement requirements.

levels.Emerging: Applies prescribed procedures to assigned lease or liability transactions.
levels.Developing: Records routine lease and other liability transactions accurately.
levels.Proficient: Reviews lease classification and related accounting entries where applicable.
levels.Advanced: Provides technical guidance on complex lease, provision, and contingent-liability matters.

dimensions.name: Interest, Repayment and Cash-Flow Recording
dimensions.definition: The ability to distinguish and accurately record interest, principal repayment, and other liability-related cash flows and reconcile the resulting balances.

levels.Emerging: Distinguishes routine liability-related cash flows under guidance.
levels.Developing: Records interest and repayment components using prescribed treatment.
levels.Proficient: Reviews interest, repayment, and related reconciliations for accuracy.
levels.Advanced: Oversees resolution of material discrepancies affecting liability cash-flow information.

dimensions.name: Monitoring and Reconciliation
dimensions.definition: The ability to monitor liability balances, perform reconciliations, analyze discrepancies and trends, and identify significant accounting or control risks.

levels.Emerging: Performs assigned checks of liability balances and supporting records.
levels.Developing: Reconciles routine liability balances and follows up discrepancies.
levels.Proficient: Analyzes liability trends, reconciliations, and supporting records to identify risks.

levels.Emerging: Collects and checks information for data interpretation and audit evidence using approved sources and basic analytical procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine data interpretation and audit evidence independently, identifies discrepancies and documents analytical results.
levels.Proficient: Applies appropriate techniques to complex data interpretation and audit evidence, interprets anomalies and trends, and develops evidence-based conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction in data interpretation and audit evidence, improves analytical methods and strengthens data-informed audit decisions.

dimensions.name: Management Information and Reporting Analysis
dimensions.definition: Uses relevant reports, performance information and operational data to evaluate results, identify issues and support evidence-based audit recommendations.

levels.Emerging: Collects and checks information for management information and reporting analysis using approved sources and basic analytical procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine management information and reporting analysis independently, identifies discrepancies and documents analytical results.
levels.Proficient: Applies appropriate techniques to complex management information and reporting analysis, interprets anomalies and trends, and develops evidence-based conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction in management information and reporting analysis, improves analytical methods and strengthens data-informed audit decisions.

competencies.name: Information Systems Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques
competencies.definition: The ability to consider information-technology risks and controls in audit engagements, apply or support computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs), evaluate automated or hybrid environments, and promote appropriate use of technology in audit work.

dimensions.name: IT Risk and Control Assessment
dimensions.definition: Identifies and evaluates relevant information-system risks, access controls, processing controls, data controls and other technology-related safeguards within audit scope.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic technology risks relevant to it risk and control assessment and follows approved tools and procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies routine technology-enabled procedures for it risk and control assessment with increasing independence and documents results.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex it risk and control assessment, selects appropriate techniques and assesses implications for audit conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Leads improvements in it risk and control assessment, mentors staff, pilots appropriate technologies and strengthens IT-audit capability.

dimensions.name: Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques
dimensions.definition: Uses or supports appropriate CAATs and technology-enabled procedures to improve the coverage, efficiency, accuracy and quality of audit work.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic technology risks relevant to computer-assisted audit techniques and follows approved tools and procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies routine technology-enabled procedures for computer-assisted audit techniques with increasing independence and documents results.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex computer-assisted audit techniques, selects appropriate techniques and assesses implications for audit conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Leads improvements in computer-assisted audit techniques, mentors staff, pilots appropriate technologies and strengthens IT-audit capability.

dimensions.name: Automated and Hybrid Environment Auditing
dimensions.definition: Adapts audit procedures to manual, automated and hybrid environments and evaluates how systems affect information reliability and control effectiveness.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic technology risks relevant to automated and hybrid environment auditing and follows approved tools and procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies routine technology-enabled procedures for automated and hybrid environment auditing with increasing independence and documents results.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex automated and hybrid environment auditing, selects appropriate techniques and assesses implications for audit conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Leads improvements in automated and hybrid environment auditing, mentors staff, pilots appropriate technologies and strengthens IT-audit capability.

dimensions.name: Audit Automation and Data Analytics
dimensions.definition: Identifies audit procedures suitable for automation or enhanced analytics and supports controlled pilots or improvements in technology-enabled auditing.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic technology risks relevant to audit automation and data analytics and follows approved tools and procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies routine technology-enabled procedures for audit automation and data analytics with increasing independence and documents results.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex audit automation and data analytics, selects appropriate techniques and assesses implications for audit conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Leads improvements in audit automation and data analytics, mentors staff, pilots appropriate technologies and strengthens IT-audit capability.

dimensions.name: IT Audit Quality and Governance
dimensions.definition: Ensures technology-assisted audit work produces practical, well-documented outputs and remains subject to appropriate quality control, independence and professional judgment.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes basic technology risks relevant to it audit quality and governance and follows approved tools and procedures.
levels.Developing: Applies routine technology-enabled procedures for it audit quality and governance with increasing independence and documents results.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex it audit quality and governance, selects appropriate techniques and assesses implications for audit conclusions.
levels.Advanced: Leads improvements in it audit quality and governance, mentors staff, pilots appropriate technologies and strengthens IT-audit capability.

competencies.name: Asset, Resource and Performance Assurance
competencies.definition: The ability to evaluate the safeguarding and proper use of government assets and resources and assess whether organizational units, programs and responsible personnel perform assigned functions effectively and in accordance with approved objectives.

dimensions.name: Asset Safeguarding and Accountability
dimensions.definition: Assesses controls for the custody, utilization, recording and safeguarding of government property, supplies, funds and other resources.

levels.Emerging: Assists with asset safeguarding and accountability using established checklists, records and inspection procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine asset safeguarding and accountability with some independence and identifies discrepancies or performance issues.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex asset safeguarding and accountability, assesses significance and recommends practical corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction for asset safeguarding and accountability, improves assurance methods and promotes stronger accountability and resource stewardship.

dimensions.name: Resource Utilization and Efficiency
dimensions.definition: Evaluates whether resources are used economically, efficiently and consistently with approved purposes and operational requirements.

levels.Emerging: Assists with resource utilization and efficiency using established checklists, records and inspection procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine resource utilization and efficiency with some independence and identifies discrepancies or performance issues.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex resource utilization and efficiency, assesses significance and recommends practical corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction for resource utilization and efficiency, improves assurance methods and promotes stronger accountability and resource stewardship.

dimensions.name: Physical Inventory and Validation
dimensions.definition: Conducts or supports physical inventory, inspection and validation activities and reconciles observed conditions with available records.

levels.Emerging: Assists with physical inventory and validation using established checklists, records and inspection procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine physical inventory and validation with some independence and identifies discrepancies or performance issues.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex physical inventory and validation, assesses significance and recommends practical corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction for physical inventory and validation, improves assurance methods and promotes stronger accountability and resource stewardship.

dimensions.name: Performance and Responsibility Assessment
dimensions.definition: Evaluates whether groups or individuals carry out assigned responsibilities effectively, based on approved standards, objectives and evidence.

levels.Emerging: Assists with performance and responsibility assessment using established checklists, records and inspection procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine performance and responsibility assessment with some independence and identifies discrepancies or performance issues.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex performance and responsibility assessment, assesses significance and recommends practical corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction for performance and responsibility assessment, improves assurance methods and promotes stronger accountability and resource stewardship.

dimensions.name: Performance Improvement and Corrective Action
dimensions.definition: Identifies performance deficiencies and recommends practical actions that strengthen accountability, efficiency and achievement of organizational objectives.

levels.Emerging: Assists with performance improvement and corrective action using established checklists, records and inspection procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine performance improvement and corrective action with some independence and identifies discrepancies or performance issues.
levels.Proficient: Independently evaluates complex performance improvement and corrective action, assesses significance and recommends practical corrective action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction for performance improvement and corrective action, improves assurance methods and promotes stronger accountability and resource stewardship.

competencies.name: Fraud Risk, Irregularity Detection and Special Investigations
competencies.definition: The ability to identify indicators of fraud, misuse, dishonesty and irregular transactions; perform protective audit functions; and support authorized special audits or investigations in a professional, objective and evidence-based manner.

dimensions.name: Fraud Risk Indicators and Red Flags
dimensions.definition: Recognizes indicators, patterns and circumstances associated with fraud, misuse, dishonesty, conflicts of interest or irregular transactions.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common indicators relevant to fraud risk indicators and red flags and follows confidentiality, evidence-handling and escalation procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine fraud risk indicators and red flags with increasing independence, documents evidence and escalates significant concerns.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex fraud risk indicators and red flags within authority, evaluates evidence, maintains objectivity and coordinates required action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership in fraud risk indicators and red flags, mentors auditors, strengthens protective controls and improves investigative capability.

dimensions.name: Fraud Prevention and Protective Controls
dimensions.definition: Assesses preventive and detective controls and recommends measures that reduce opportunities for fraud, misuse and loss of government resources.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common indicators relevant to fraud prevention and protective controls and follows confidentiality, evidence-handling and escalation procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine fraud prevention and protective controls with increasing independence, documents evidence and escalates significant concerns.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex fraud prevention and protective controls within authority, evaluates evidence, maintains objectivity and coordinates required action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership in fraud prevention and protective controls, mentors auditors, strengthens protective controls and improves investigative capability.

dimensions.name: Irregular Transaction Review
dimensions.definition: Examines unusual, questionable or risk-prone transactions and develops evidence-based observations for appropriate action or escalation.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common indicators relevant to irregular transaction review and follows confidentiality, evidence-handling and escalation procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine irregular transaction review with increasing independence, documents evidence and escalates significant concerns.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex irregular transaction review within authority, evaluates evidence, maintains objectivity and coordinates required action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership in irregular transaction review, mentors auditors, strengthens protective controls and improves investigative capability.

dimensions.name: Special Audit and Investigation Support
dimensions.definition: Performs or supports special audits and investigations when duly authorized, following approved scope, procedures, confidentiality and evidentiary requirements.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common indicators relevant to special audit and investigation support and follows confidentiality, evidence-handling and escalation procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine special audit and investigation support with increasing independence, documents evidence and escalates significant concerns.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex special audit and investigation support within authority, evaluates evidence, maintains objectivity and coordinates required action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership in special audit and investigation support, mentors auditors, strengthens protective controls and improves investigative capability.

dimensions.name: External Agency Coordination
dimensions.definition: Coordinates, when authorized, with COA, DBM, DOJ or other relevant agencies while maintaining proper authority, documentation, confidentiality and audit independence.

levels.Emerging: Recognizes common indicators relevant to external agency coordination and follows confidentiality, evidence-handling and escalation procedures.
levels.Developing: Performs routine external agency coordination with increasing independence, documents evidence and escalates significant concerns.
levels.Proficient: Independently handles complex external agency coordination within authority, evaluates evidence, maintains objectivity and coordinates required action.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership in external agency coordination, mentors auditors, strengthens protective controls and improves investigative capability.

competencies.name: Audit Reporting, Recommendations and Follow-Up
competencies.definition: The ability to evaluate and communicate audit findings, evidence, conclusions and recommendations through clear, accurate and timely audit reports, and to monitor and validate implementation of agreed corrective actions.

dimensions.name: Audit Report Review and Endorsement
dimensions.definition: Reviews draft and final audit reports for completeness, consistency, evidence, conformity with approved scope and applicable audit standards before endorsement.

levels.Emerging: Supports audit report review and endorsement using approved report formats, evidence and guidance; checks basic completeness and accuracy.
levels.Developing: Reviews or prepares routine audit report review and endorsement with increasing independence and resolves ordinary inconsistencies.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex audit report review and endorsement, ensures evidence-to-conclusion linkage and formulates practical, SMART corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on audit report review and endorsement, mentors staff, strengthens follow-up mechanisms and promotes implementation of audit recommendations.

dimensions.name: Findings, Conclusions and Audit Opinions
dimensions.definition: Assesses whether findings and conclusions are supported by sufficient evidence and appropriately reflect the significance and implications of identified issues.

levels.Emerging: Supports findings, conclusions and audit opinions using approved report formats, evidence and guidance; checks basic completeness and accuracy.
levels.Developing: Reviews or prepares routine findings, conclusions and audit opinions with increasing independence and resolves ordinary inconsistencies.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex findings, conclusions and audit opinions, ensures evidence-to-conclusion linkage and formulates practical, SMART corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on findings, conclusions and audit opinions, mentors staff, strengthens follow-up mechanisms and promotes implementation of audit recommendations.

dimensions.name: Actionable and SMART Recommendations
dimensions.definition: Develops or improves recommendations so that corrective actions are evidence-based, practical, specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.

levels.Emerging: Supports actionable and smart recommendations using approved report formats, evidence and guidance; checks basic completeness and accuracy.
levels.Developing: Reviews or prepares routine actionable and smart recommendations with increasing independence and resolves ordinary inconsistencies.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex actionable and smart recommendations, ensures evidence-to-conclusion linkage and formulates practical, SMART corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on actionable and smart recommendations, mentors staff, strengthens follow-up mechanisms and promotes implementation of audit recommendations.

dimensions.name: Audit Communication and Stakeholder Discussion
dimensions.definition: Communicates audit results professionally, discusses significant findings with concerned stakeholders and facilitates constructive dialogue on practical corrective actions.

levels.Emerging: Supports audit communication and stakeholder discussion using approved report formats, evidence and guidance; checks basic completeness and accuracy.
levels.Developing: Reviews or prepares routine audit communication and stakeholder discussion with increasing independence and resolves ordinary inconsistencies.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex audit communication and stakeholder discussion, ensures evidence-to-conclusion linkage and formulates practical, SMART corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on audit communication and stakeholder discussion, mentors staff, strengthens follow-up mechanisms and promotes implementation of audit recommendations.

dimensions.name: Recommendation Monitoring and Validation
dimensions.definition: Monitors and validates the status of management actions, documents implementation evidence, identifies unresolved matters and supports reporting of follow-up results.

levels.Emerging: Supports recommendation monitoring and validation using approved report formats, evidence and guidance; checks basic completeness and accuracy.
levels.Developing: Reviews or prepares routine recommendation monitoring and validation with increasing independence and resolves ordinary inconsistencies.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex recommendation monitoring and validation, ensures evidence-to-conclusion linkage and formulates practical, SMART corrective actions.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert direction on recommendation monitoring and validation, mentors staff, strengthens follow-up mechanisms and promotes implementation of audit recommendations.

competencies.name: Responsive Audit Management, Professional Communication and Stakeholder Liaison
competencies.definition: The ability to deliver audit services responsively and professionally while maintaining objectivity, confidentiality, impartiality and independence; coordinate with auditees and oversight bodies; and contribute to the credibility and continuous improvement of the audit function.

dimensions.name: Stakeholder Engagement and Responsiveness
dimensions.definition: Engages relevant stakeholders throughout the audit process, understands operational context and responds appropriately to legitimate concerns within the approved audit scope.

levels.Emerging: Communicates and coordinates appropriately for stakeholder engagement and responsiveness using established protocols and maintains confidentiality and professionalism.
levels.Developing: Handles routine to moderately complex stakeholder engagement and responsiveness with increasing independence and adapts communication to stakeholders.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex stakeholder engagement and responsiveness, anticipates stakeholder concerns, exercises professional judgment and protects audit independence.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership for stakeholder engagement and responsiveness, builds institutional trust, mentors staff and improves stakeholder and oversight coordination.

dimensions.name: Professional Communication and Presentation
dimensions.definition: Presents audit plans, findings, conclusions and recommendations clearly and appropriately to staff, management and other authorized stakeholders.

levels.Emerging: Communicates and coordinates appropriately for professional communication and presentation using established protocols and maintains confidentiality and professionalism.
levels.Developing: Handles routine to moderately complex professional communication and presentation with increasing independence and adapts communication to stakeholders.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex professional communication and presentation, anticipates stakeholder concerns, exercises professional judgment and protects audit independence.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership for professional communication and presentation, builds institutional trust, mentors staff and improves stakeholder and oversight coordination.

dimensions.name: Policy and Regulatory Interpretation
dimensions.definition: Interprets applicable audit rules, policies, standards and guidance, clarifies issues and refers matters to appropriate authorities when outside delegated responsibility.

levels.Emerging: Communicates and coordinates appropriately for policy and regulatory interpretation using established protocols and maintains confidentiality and professionalism.
levels.Developing: Handles routine to moderately complex policy and regulatory interpretation with increasing independence and adapts communication to stakeholders.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex policy and regulatory interpretation, anticipates stakeholder concerns, exercises professional judgment and protects audit independence.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership for policy and regulatory interpretation, builds institutional trust, mentors staff and improves stakeholder and oversight coordination.

dimensions.name: Oversight and Inter-Audit Coordination
dimensions.definition: Liaises with COA, DBM and other authorized oversight or review bodies and coordinates appropriately to maximize audit coverage and minimize unnecessary duplication.

levels.Emerging: Communicates and coordinates appropriately for oversight and inter-audit coordination using established protocols and maintains confidentiality and professionalism.
levels.Developing: Handles routine to moderately complex oversight and inter-audit coordination with increasing independence and adapts communication to stakeholders.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex oversight and inter-audit coordination, anticipates stakeholder concerns, exercises professional judgment and protects audit independence.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership for oversight and inter-audit coordination, builds institutional trust, mentors staff and improves stakeholder and oversight coordination.

dimensions.name: Professionalism, Independence and Continuous Learning
dimensions.definition: Maintains due professional care, objectivity, impartiality and confidentiality; pursues continuing professional development and applies lessons learned to improve audit performance.

levels.Emerging: Communicates and coordinates appropriately for professionalism, independence and continuous learning using established protocols and maintains confidentiality and professionalism.
levels.Developing: Handles routine to moderately complex professionalism, independence and continuous learning with increasing independence and adapts communication to stakeholders.
levels.Proficient: Independently manages complex professionalism, independence and continuous learning, anticipates stakeholder concerns, exercises professional judgment and protects audit independence.
levels.Advanced: Provides expert leadership for professionalism, independence and continuous learning, builds institutional trust, mentors staff and improves stakeholder and oversight coordination.

levels.Emerging:
Recognizes basic GEDSI concepts and applies relevant policies in assigned work.
• Considers the needs and perspectives of diverse groups when performing routine duties.
• Uses appropriate sex-, disability- or social-inclusion information when relevant to assigned work.
levels.Developing:
Applies GEDSI principles in project activities and stakeholder interactions.
• Recognizes potential exclusion or accessibility concerns and raises them for appropriate action.
• Supports collection and use of relevant disaggregated information when required.
levels.Proficient:
Integrates GEDSI considerations into project planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation.
• Identifies and addresses barriers affecting women, persons with disabilities and other marginalized groups.
• Provides practical inputs that improve inclusivity, accessibility and responsiveness of project activities.
levels.Advanced:
Provides technical guidance on GEDSI-responsive policies, programs, mechanisms and facilities.
• Advises or coaches others on GEDSI and promotes inclusive project and organizational practices.
• Champions sustainable GEDSI initiatives and integrates diverse perspectives into higher-level project and policy decisions.
